articles.title: Italy World Cup winner and AC Milan legend Franco Baresi dies aged 66
articles.summary: Franco Baresi, who won the World Cup with Italy and was regarded as one of football's finest defenders, dies aged 66.
articles.titleZh: 意大利世界杯冠军、AC米兰传奇人物弗朗哥·巴雷西去世，享年 66 岁
articles.summaryZh: 弗朗哥·巴雷西 (Franco Baresi) 去世，享年 66 岁，他曾随意大利队夺得世界杯冠军，被视为足球界最优秀的后卫之一。

contentParagraphs.en: Franco Baresi, the former AC Milan captain who was one of Italy’s most acclaimed defenders, has died. He was 66.His death was announced on Friday by Milan, the football club where he spent his entire 20-year playing career. No cause of death was given.Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the FIFA World Cup: All to knowlist 2 of 4What has FIFA charged Argentina with, and what could the punishment be?list 3 of 4Storm apologize after co-owner berates teen girls for support of Cunninghamlist 4 of 4Viral finger-clicker suspended as cricket storm remains in global spotlightend of list“The entire history of AC Milan is in tears,” Milan said.In August 2025, Baresi underwent surgery to remove a pulmonary nodule and subsequently began a course of immunotherapy.His last public appearance was at the opening ceremony for the Milano Cortina Winter Olympics in February, when, along with former Inter Milan defender Giuseppe Bergomi, he carried the torch into the San Siro — the stadium he formerly played in.“His example and integrity will be forever etched into the Club’s DNA, just as his iconic number 6 shirt is,” Milan added. “The condolences AC Milan extends to Franco Baresi’s family at such a difficult time are shared by every Rossonero, who feels this loss as their own.”Baresi was on Italy’s team that won the World Cup in 1982.“With the passing of Franco Baresi, Italy loses not only one of the greatest champions in its sports history, but also an example of loyalty, professionalism, and dedication,” Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni said on X.One-club player Baresi etched in AC Milan historyBaresi, who was widely regarded as one of the best defenders of all time, was a true one-club player. He progressed through the ranks at Milan and made his first team debut at the age of 17, in April 1978.He chose to stay with Milan even after it was relegated to Serie B — for the second time in three seasons — in 1982, just before he helped Italy win the World Cup that summer, and was given the captaincy at the age of just 22.Baresi made more than 700 appearances for the Rossoneri, captaining the team to global dominance in the late 1980s and early 1990s.With Milan, Baresi won three Champions League trophies, six Serie A titles, two Intercontinental Cups, three European Supercups and four Italian Supercups.“For generations, Franco embodied the values, character and excellence that define this club,” Milan owner Gerry Cardinale said. “Even as he battled his greatest challenge over the last year, he was always there for the club, quietly reminding us all what it means to wear these colours.“Franco’s legacy is profound and will endure forever. Our thoughts are with his family and all those whose lives he touched.”In his final interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport last year, Baresi said he recalled being a “Milanista” (Milan fan) as a child.“When I arrived at Milanello (Milan’s training centre) for the first time as a 14-year-old, it seemed like entering paradise,” Baresi said.Franco Baresi of Italy in action against Romario of Brazil at World Cup 1994 [Action Images/Reuters]Baresi the first to have AC Milan jersey retiredAs well as the 1982 World Cup, Baresi also helped Italy finish runners-up in the 1994 competition — although he was one of three Azzurri players to miss a penalty in the shootout defeat to Brazil in the final.Baresi finished runner-up to teammate Marco van Basten in the Ballon d’Or awards in 1989.When Baresi retired in 1997, Milan also retired his No 6 jersey — which was a first for Italian football. The club also held a celebration match in his honour, featuring many football stars Baresi had played with and against.Baresi was made honorary president of Milan in 2020.“Italian soccer has lost one of its legends,” Italian football federation president Giovanni Malago said, labelling Baresi “an extraordinary champion who wore only two shirts for his entire career: those of Milan and Italy”.“We will have a tribute to remember him the next time the national team plays,” Malago added.How Inter Milan missed out to AC on BaresiIt could have all been so different for Baresi and Milan, however. Baresi had trials at Inter when he was younger but he was rejected by the Nerazzurri, who opted to sign his older brother Giuseppe Baresi, with Franco going on to join the youth team of their fierce city rivals.Giuseppe also captained his team and the image of the two Baresi brothers exchanging pennants before kickoff became the symbol of the Milan derby throughout the late 80s.“On November 19, 1995, I made my Serie A debut against Milan. I was 17 years old, and on the other side was the captain of that team: Franco Baresi,” former Italy captain Gianluigi Buffon said on X, referring to his Italian league debut with Parma.“For a boy my age, finding myself on the field against champions like him was something incredible,” Buffon added. “From that day on, I had an even clearer understanding of what it meant to represent football with class, leadership, and respect. Ciao Franco. Rest in peace.”
contentParagraphs.zh: 前 AC 米兰队长、意大利最受赞誉的后卫之一弗朗哥·巴雷西去世。他享年 66 岁。周五，他在米兰足球俱乐部度过了 20 年的职业生涯，宣布了他的去世消息。没有给出死亡原因。推荐故事列表 4 项列表 1（共 4）因凡蒂诺出售 FIFA 世界杯股份的计划：众所周知列表 2（共 4）国际足联对阿根廷提出了什么指控，以及可能的处罚是什么？列表 3（共 4）风暴在共同所有人斥责青少年女孩支持坎宁安后道歉列表 4（共 4）由于板球风暴仍然受到全球关注，病毒手指点击游戏被暂停，列表末尾“整个历史”米兰说道。2025 年 8 月，巴雷西接受了肺结节切除手术，随后开始了免疫治疗。他最后一次公开露面是在 2 月份的米兰科尔蒂纳冬奥会开幕式上，当时他与前国际米兰后卫朱塞佩·贝尔戈米一起将火炬传递到了他曾经效力过的圣西罗球场。“他的榜样和正直将永远铭刻在俱乐部的 DNA 中，就像他的标志性人物一样6号球衣是，”米兰补充道。 “在如此困难的时刻，AC米兰向弗朗哥·巴雷西的家人表示哀悼，这是每一位红黑球员的共同感受，他们都将这次损失视为自己的损失。”巴雷西是1982年意大利世界杯冠军队的成员。“随着弗朗哥·巴雷西的去世，意大利不仅失去了体育史上最伟大的冠军之一，而且还失去了忠诚、专业和奉献的典范，”意大利总理乔治亚·梅洛尼在接受《X.One-club》球员采访时说道。巴雷西铭刻AC米兰历史 巴雷西被广泛认为是有史以来最好的后卫之一，是一位真正的一家具乐部球员。他在米兰不断进步，并于 1978 年 4 月在 17 岁的时候首次代表一线队亮相。尽管米兰在 1982 年三年内第二次降级到乙级联赛，但他还是选择留在米兰，就在他帮助意大利赢得那年夏天的世界杯之前，年仅 22 岁的他就被任命为队长。巴雷西为红黑军团出场超过 700 场，带领球队走向世界各地。巴雷西在 1980 年代末和 90 年代初占据统治地位。在米兰，巴雷西赢得了 3 座欧冠奖杯、6 座意甲冠军、2 座洲际杯、3 座欧洲超级杯和 4 座意大利超级杯。“对于几代人来说，佛朗哥体现了定义这家具乐部的价值观、性格和卓越，”米兰老板格里·卡迪纳尔说道。 “即使他去年面临着最大的挑战，他也始终为俱乐部而战，静静地提醒我们所有人穿着这些颜色意味着什么。“弗朗哥的遗产是深远的，并将永远持续下去。我们的思念与他的家人以及所有被他影响过的人同在。”去年接受《米兰体育报》采访时，巴雷西表示，他回忆起了小时候的“米兰斯塔”（米兰球迷）。“当我14岁时第一次来到米兰内洛（米兰的训练中心）时，感觉就像进入了天堂，”巴雷西说道。 1994年世界杯，意大利队的弗兰科·巴雷西对阵巴西队的罗马里奥[动作图片/路透社]巴雷西是第一个退役AC米兰球衣的人 除了1982年世界杯，巴雷西还在1994年世界杯上帮助意大利获得亚军——尽管他是决赛中点球大战输给巴西时错失点球的三名蓝衣军团球员之一。巴雷西在1989年的金球奖中不敌队友马可·范巴斯滕获得亚军。 1997 年，米兰还退役了他的 6 号球衣，这也是意大利足球史上的第一次。俱乐部还为他举办了一场庆祝比赛，许多与巴雷西一起并肩作战的足球明星都参加了比赛。巴雷西于 2020 年被任命为米兰名誉主席。“意大利足球失去了一位传奇人物，”意大利足协主席乔瓦尼·马拉戈表示，巴雷西是“一位非凡的冠军，他的整个职业生涯只穿了两件球衣：米兰的球衣和米兰的球衣。”马拉戈补充道：“下次国家队比赛时，我们会向他致敬。国际米兰如何错过巴雷西的AC米兰。然而，对于巴雷西和米兰来说，一切可能都是如此不同。巴雷西年轻时曾在国际米兰试训，但他被蓝黑军团拒绝了，蓝黑军团选择签下他的哥哥朱塞佩·巴雷西，佛朗哥随后加入了他们激烈的同城对手的青年队。朱塞佩还担任过他的球队和意大利国家队的队长。巴雷西两兄弟在开球前交换锦旗的画面成为了整个80年代末米兰德比的标志。 “1995年11月19日，我在对阵米兰的比赛中完成了意甲首秀。 “我当时 17 岁，另一边是那支球队的队长：佛朗哥·巴雷西。”前意大利队队长吉安路易吉·布冯在 X 上谈到他在帕尔马的意大利联赛首秀时说道。“对于我这个年纪的男孩来说，发现自己在球场上对阵像他这样的冠军是一件令人难以置信的事情，”布冯补充道。“从那天起，我更加清楚地了解了代表足球意味着阶级、领导力和尊重意味着什么。”你好弗朗哥。安息。”

articles.title: AI labels to be compulsory on authentic-looking content under EU rules
articles.summary:
Companies must ensure people know when they are interacting with artificially generated images, audio and text designed to look real
From apparently conspiring to steal elections to abusing staff or performing embarrassing dance moves, the last few years have seen plenty of fake
articles.titleZh: 根据欧盟规则，人工智能标签将强制出现在真实内容上
articles.summaryZh:
公司必须确保人们知道他们何时与人工生成的图像、音频和文本进行交互，这些图像、音频和文本旨在看起来真实
从明显密谋窃取选举到辱骂工作人员或表演令人尴尬的舞蹈动作，过去几年出现了很多假选举

contentParagraphs.en: From apparently conspiring to steal elections to abusing staff or performing embarrassing dance moves, the last few years have seen plenty of fake content made about politicians intended to malign its targets and mislead the public.Now EU rules aim to stem the flood of this deceptive content: starting from Sunday, artificially generated images, audio and text designed to look authentic must be labelled.The rules, devised under the EU’s landmark AI Act, mean companies must ensure people know when they are interacting with an AI-powered chatbot or viewing a manipulated image or AI-generated text.Deep fakes have included fake audio of the Slovakian opposition leader, Michal Šimečka, conspiring with a journalist to rig election. Photograph: Radovan Stoklasa/ReutersThe rules apply to new AI systems on the EU market from 2 August, while existing ones have an extra four months to comply.“It is a matter not only of customer protection, it’s also a matter of democracy protection,” the Green MEP Sergey Lagodinsky, who helped negotiate the AI Act, told the Guardian. “Making transparent this information is something which we need to preserve our democracy and the authenticity of facts online.”Under the rules, synthetic text, images, video and audio designed to look truthful must be visibly marked as AI-generated and contain a digital watermark to show the artificial origins of the content.Texts on matters of public interest must also be labelled as AI-made if there is no human editorial oversight.Companies are encouraged to label AI-generated content pre-dating the rules, although this is not compulsory. The rules will not apply to users’ personal content and there is an exemption for “evidently artistic”, satirical and fictional works.Failure to comply could result in fines of up to €15m or 3% of a company’s worldwide global turnover.The EU executive has created black-and-white labels anyone can use, although companies can design their own.EU symbols to be used on content using AI. Illustration: EUDeep fakes have included audio purporting to reveal the Slovakian opposition leader Michal Šimečka conspiring with a journalist to rig elections, mocked-up videos of the French president, Emmanuel Macron, dancing in a 1980s nightclub, and fake footage of the then UK Labour leader Keir Starmer abusing party staff.The tech industry says it supports the quest to make deep fakes visible, but fears the rules will be interpreted too broadly and overwhelm internet users with banners and labels.The Computer and Communications Industry Association argues that EU guidelines published in July have expanded the definition of a deep fake far beyond the 2024 AI Act.“The label was meant to flag deceptive content,” CCIA Europe’s AI policy lead, Boniface de Champris, said. “That distinction has been removed, so now almost everything gets labelled – a landscape in an advert is the same as a manipulated political speech. Like cookie banners, once labels are everywhere, users stop noticing them. That doesn’t protect anyone, it just burdens commercial activity across the board.”He thinks the most visible change for the public will not be on social media, which “already labels most AI content” but “in areas where AI is already used at scale but people don’t know it – advertising, film, publishing”.“Expect a lot more labels in sectors not usually associated with AI, and the burden will fall hardest on those least versed in AI regulation,” De Champris said.Some of the world’s largest tech companies already have policies to inform users about AI-generated content.TikTok, for example, requires creators to label realistic AI-generated images, audio and video, and says it has helped label more than 3bn pieces of content.Google launched a tool called SynthID in 2023, which enables users to check if an image is AI-generated. The company says it has put an invisible digital watermark, which enables identification, on more than 100bn images and 60,000 years’ worth of audio.Google and Meta, which owns Facebook and Instagram, have signed a voluntary code of practice intended to help companies comply with the EU’s AI transparency rules.The European Commission said more than 180 organisations had signed the code, which was drawn up by independent experts under the supervision of the EU AI office.Signing the code is seen by regulators as a sign of good intent, while non-signatories must show they are meeting the rules in other ways.Meta launched policies in 2024 to help people identify AI-generated photo-realistic images. It says it has been developing industry-wide technical standards to identify AI audio and video.Announcing Meta’s intention to sign the EU code of practice earlier this week [28 July], vice president for public policy in Europe, Markus Reinisch, said: “We must avoid a situation where online content is subject to a growing array of different labels and disclosures that end up overwhelming people, while at the same time adding additional regulatory complexity for providers.”Lagodinsky, the EU lawmaker, said he believed the industry could find a way: “I have a deep respect for industry, but in all too many cases, they complain, and… then after things are implemented, it doesn’t look that burdensome to them. And there is always a solution.”The transparency rules are part of broader enforcement of the AI Act, starting from 2 August. The Commission’s lead official on tech policy, Henna Virkkunen, said AI was a “transformative technology” that can bring extraordinary benefits” but the most advanced models “create risks on an entirely new scale”.“Europe anticipated this development. With the AI Act, we established a clear, risk-based and durable framework for trustworthy AI —one that gives innovators legal certainty while protecting the public interest.”
contentParagraphs.zh: 从明显密谋窃取选举到虐待员工或表演令人尴尬的舞蹈动作，过去几年出现了大量关于政客意图诽谤其目标并误导公众的虚假内容。现在，欧盟的规定旨在阻止这种欺骗性内容的泛滥：从周日开始，人工生成的图像、音频和文本设计得看起来真实，必须被贴上标签。这些规则是根据欧盟具有里程碑意义的人工智能法案制定的，这意味着公司必须确保人们知道他们何时与人工智能交互聊天机器人或查看经过处理的图像或人工智能生成的文本。深度造假包括斯洛伐克反对派领导人米哈尔·西梅奇卡 (Michal Šimečka) 与一名记者合谋操纵选举的虚假音频。照片：Radovan Stoklasa/Reuters 这些规则从 8 月 2 日起适用于欧盟市场上的新人工智能系统，而现有系统有额外四个月的时间来遵守。“这不仅是客户保护的问题，也是民主保护的问题，”帮助谈判人工智能法案的绿党议员谢尔盖·拉戈丁斯基 (Sergey Lagodinsky) 告诉卫报。 “我们需要使这些信息变得透明，以维护我们的民主和在线事实的真实性。”根据规则，旨在看起来真实的合成文本、图像、视频和音频必须明显标记为人工智能生成的，并包含数字水印以显示内容的人工来源。如果没有人工编辑监督，有关公共利益问题的文本也必须标记为人工智能生成的。鼓励公司在规则发布之前标记人工智能生成的内容，尽管这不是强制性的。这些规则不适用于用户的个人内容，并且对“明显艺术”、讽刺和虚构的作品有豁免。不遵守规定可能会导致高达 1500 万欧元或公司全球营业额 3% 的罚款。欧盟行政部门创建了任何人都可以使用的黑白标签，尽管公司可以设计自己的。使用人工智能在内容上使用欧盟符号。插图：EUDeep 虚假内容包括声称揭露斯洛伐克反对党领袖 Michal Šimečka 与记者合谋操纵选举的音频、法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙 (Emmanuel Macron) 在 1980 年代夜总会跳舞的模拟视频，以及时任英国工党领袖凯尔·斯塔默 (Keir Starmer) 虐待党内工作人员的虚假镜头。科技行业表示，它支持让 Deep Fake 可见的努力，但担心这些规则会被解释得太宽泛。计算机和通信行业协会认为，7 月发布的欧盟指导方针扩大了深度造假的定义，远远超出了 2024 年人工智能法案的范围。“该标签的目的是标记欺骗性内容，”CCIA 欧洲人工智能政策负责人 Boniface de Champris 表示。 “这种区别已经被消除，所以现在几乎所有东西都被贴上了标签——广告中的风景与被操纵的政治演讲是一样的。就像饼干横幅一样，一旦标签无处不在，用户就不再注意到它们。这并不能保护任何人，只会给商业活动带来全面的负担。”他认为，对公众来说最明显的变化不是在社交媒体上，社交媒体“已经给大多数人工智能内容贴上标签”，而是“在人工智能已经大规模使用但人们不知道的领域——广告、电影、 De Champris 表示：“预计通常与 AI 无关的行业将会出现更多标签，而那些最不熟悉 AI 监管的人将承受最沉重的负担。”世界上一些最大的科技公司已经制定了政策，向用户告知 AI 生成的内容。例如，TikTok 要求创作者对真实的 AI 生成的图像、音频和视频进行标记，并表示它已帮助标记了超过 30 亿条内容。Google 在 2023 年推出了一款名为 SynthID 的工具，该工具使用户能够检查如果图像是人工智能生成的。该公司表示，它已在超过 1000 亿张图像和 6 万年的音频中添加了可识别的隐形数字水印。谷歌和 Facebook 和 Instagram 的母公司 Meta 签署了一份自愿行为准则，旨在帮助企业遵守欧盟人工智能透明度规则。欧盟委员会表示，已有 180 多个组织签署了该准则，该准则是由独立专家在欧盟人工智能办公室的监督下起草的。监管机构将签署该准则视为良好的意图，而非签署者必须证明他们以其他方式遵守规则。Meta 于 2024 年推出了政策，帮助人们识别人工智能生成的照片级真实图像。它表示一直在制定全行业技术标准来识别人工智能音频和视频。 欧洲公共政策副总裁 Markus Reinisch 于本周早些时候（7 月 28 日）宣布 Meta 打算签署欧盟行为准则，他表示：“我们必须避免在线内容受到越来越多的不同标签和披露的影响，最终使人们不知所措，同时增加了提供商的额外监管复杂性。”欧盟立法者 Lagodinsky 表示，他相信该行业可以找到一个解决方案方式：“我对行业怀有深深的敬意，但在太多情况下，他们会抱怨，然后......事情实施后，对他们来说看起来并不那么麻烦。而且总有解决方案。”透明度规则是从 8 月 2 日开始更广泛执行《人工智能法案》的一部分。欧盟委员会技术政策首席官员 Henna Virkkunen 表示，人工智能是一项“变革性技术”，可以带来非凡的好处”，但最先进的模型“会带来全新规模的风险”。“欧洲预计到了这一发展。通过《人工智能法案》，我们为值得信赖的人工智能建立了一个清晰的、基于风险的持久框架——为创新者提供法律确定性，同时保护公共利益。”

articles.title: Sainsbury's agrees to sell Argos for £120m
articles.summary: Under the terms of the deal, Argos will still operate in Sainsbury's shops, sell Habitat products, and offer Nectar points.
articles.titleZh: Sainsbury's 同意以 1.2 亿英镑出售 Argos
articles.summaryZh: 根据交易条款，Argos 仍将在 Sainsbury 的商店中运营、销售 Habitat 产品并提供 Nectar 积分。

contentParagraphs.en: Sainsbury's has agreed to sell Argos for £120m after a long process of trying to offload it as the supermarket chain aims to focus on its main food business.Sainsbury's said it would be "business as usual" for Argos customers, staff, and suppliers. Shoppers will see no change as Argos will still operate in Sainsbury's shops, sell Habitat products, and offer Nectar points.The buyer, Swift Partners, is a company that has been created to buy the brand and includes former Co-operative Group boss Richard Pennycook.There are 667 Argos shops across the UK, with 201 operating as standalone stores and 466 operating within Sainsbury's. It also has more than 450 collection points.Founded in 1973, Argos opened shops where customers browsed its catalogues and placed their orders, with products being delivered to tills from warehouses connected to the stores.The Argos catalogue, once described by comedian Bill Bailey as the "laminated book of dreams", used to be a physical book.Argos no longer prints this hefty tome, with its full range now available online instead. In store, customers can browse the product collection on tablet computers.Sainsbury's has been trying to sell Argos - which has been seen as an underperforming brand - for some time.Sainsbury's bought Argos – together with Habitat and all the other retail brands owned by Home Retail Group – in 2016 for £1.4bn. It then sold Argos financial services, which runs the Argos card, for around £720m in 2024.In September last year, its talks to sell the rest of Argos to Chinese online retailer JD.com fell through.Sainsbury's chief executive Simon Robert said that all of Argos's nearly 14,000 staff would be transferred over to Swift Partners as part of the deal.He also confirmed that Argos would continue to operate in Sainsbury's shops; Nectar will continue to be used across both Argos and Sainsbury's; and Sainsbury's will continue to sell Habitat productsSwift Partners' Pennycook said he believed "strongly in Argos's future and see real opportunities to invest and build on its progress".The deal is expected to be completed in February next year.Pennycook said there was the potential to open new standalone Argos shops – and did not rule out the possibility of the return of its print catalogue.Retail analyst Clive Black said he had always questioned whether Argos was "wholly aligned" with Sainsbury's grocery business, describing the supermarket group's attempt to sell Argos as "challenging and prolonged".He said Argos has been a "suboptimal performer from a financial perspective".Catherine Shuttleworth, another retail analyst, said Sainsbury's had been "distracted" by its main supermarket arm and therefore unable to fully focus on Argos.However, under new ownership, she said Argos has the potential to be a "really digital-first business" capable of giving a "bloody nose" to online retail giants like Amazon.In Sainsbury's latest results for the first three months of this year, group-wide sales were up 3.1%, although sales for Argos specifically had dipped 0.5%.Bally Auluk, national officer at Usdaw, a union which represents Argos workers, said the announcement would create uncertainty, but that it welcomed Swift's commitment to "keeping the model of store in stores, standalone stores and local fulfilment centres".
contentParagraphs.zh: Sainsbury’s 同意以 1.2 亿英镑的价格出售 Argos，因为这家连锁超市旨在专注于其主要食品业务。Sainsbury’s 表示，对于 Argos 的客户、员工和供应商来说，这将是“一切照常”。购物者不会看到任何变化，因为 Argos 仍将在 Sainsbury's 商店运营，销售 Habitat 产品并提供 Nectar 积分。买家 Swift Partners 是一家为购买该品牌而创建的公司，其中包括前 Co-operative Group 老板 Richard Pennycook。Argos 在英国各地有 667 家商店，其中 201 家作为独立商店运营，466 家在 Sainsbury's 内运营。它还拥有 450 多个收集点。Argos 成立于 1973 年，开设了商店，顾客可以在其中浏览其目录并下订单，产品从与商店相连的仓库运送到收银台。Argos 目录曾经被喜剧演员比尔·贝利描述为“梦想的层压书”，曾经是一本实体书。Argos 不再印刷这本厚重的书，现在全系列产品都可以在网上购买。在商店里，顾客可以在平板电脑上浏览产品系列。一段时间以来，Sainsbury's 一直试图出售 Argos，该品牌一直被视为表现不佳的品牌。Sainsbury's 于 2016 年以 14 亿英镑的价格收购了 Argos，以及 Habitat 和 Home Retail Group 旗下的所有其他零售品牌。随后，该公司于2024年以约7.2亿英镑的价格出售了运营Argos卡的Argos金融服务公司。去年9月，其将Argos剩余部分出售给中国在线零售商京东的谈判失败。塞恩斯伯里首席执行官西蒙·罗伯特表示，作为交易的一部分，Argos的近14,000名员工将全部转移到Swift Partners。他还证实，Argos将继续在塞恩斯伯里运营。商店； Nectar 将继续在 Argos 和 Sainsbury's 中使用； Swift Partners 的 Pennycook 表示，他“对 Argos 的未来充满信心，看到了投资和发展的真正机会”。该交易预计将于明年 2 月完成。Pennycook 表示，有可能开设新的独立 Argos 商店，并且不排除归还其印刷目录的可能性。零售分析师 Clive Black 表示，他一直质疑 Argos 是否与 Argos“完全一致”。 Sainsbury's 的杂货业务将超市集团出售 Argos 的尝试描述为“具有挑战性且旷日持久”。他表示，Argos 一直是“从财务角度来看表现欠佳”。另一位零售分析师 Catherine Shuttleworth 表示，Sainsbury's 已被其主要超市部门“分散了注意力”，因此无法完全专注于 Argos。然而，在新的所有权下，她表示 Argos 有潜力成为“真正的数字优先企业”，能够让像亚马逊这样的在线零售巨头“流鼻血”。在塞恩斯伯里今年前三个月的最新业绩中，整个集团的销售额增长了3.1%，尽管Argos的销售额具体下降了0.5%。代表Argos工人的工会Usdaw的全国官员巴利·奥鲁克(Bally Auluk)表示，这一公告将带来不确定性，但它欢迎斯威夫特承诺“将商店模式保留在商店、独立商店和当地履行中心”。

articles.title: Drought conditions may worsen before improving as little rain in sight
articles.summary: Conditions in the most parched areas of the United Kingdom could worsen before they improve, according to the latest forecasts.
articles.titleZh: 由于看不到降雨，干旱状况在改善之前可能会恶化
articles.summaryZh: 根据最新预测，英国最干旱地区的情况在好转之前可能会进一步恶化。

contentParagraphs.en: Parts of the UK can expect to see some rain through Friday and into the weekend, though for the areas of England and Wales under drought conditions the coming days look set to remain dry.Friday will be rather cloudy across northern areas of the UK, with the chance of some scattered showers which may be locally rather heavy.Further south, though, it looks set to be another generally dry day with variable amounts of cloud and some sunny spells. South-east England, which is officially in drought, will have another warm day.Into the weekend, the dry weather looks set to continue for most, with the exception of Scotland, which may see some isolated showers across the far north.Next week, the forecast looks more unsettled, with more of a chance of rain, though it is likely to be northwestern parts of the UK which are the wettest. Some forecast models do suggest that more southern areas may receive some useful rain, but this is much less certain.Despite some rain in the forecast in the coming week, it will not be enough to end drought conditions.When rain falls in the summer months, high daytime temperatures can mean that the water quickly evaporates away from the soil. Meanwhile, a series of quick downpours such as heavy summer showers or thunderstorms may appear to give large rainfall totals, but the rain falls faster than the soil can absorb it.The ideal scenario is for rain to fall overnight to mitigate the loss from evaporation. However, to alleviate the drought there would still need to be a prolonged spell of rain over a number of days and weeks. This means the rain forecast in the coming days is likely to do very little to quench the parched earth.Wales has received just 8% of its long-term average rainfall for July, putting it on course to be the driest July there since records began 190 years ago.Rhian Thomas, Sustainable Water and Nature Manager at NRW, said: "The toll on the environment, our land and agriculture is clear to see, with many of our teams still dealing with the aftermath of extensive wildfires which have devastated forestry, grassland and special habitats."In England, July has brought just 7% of expected rainfall, falling to 1% across southern England.On Wednesday, the Environment Agency, warned that the hot and dry weather meant people are "using water faster than nature can replenish it".Heading into August, the forecast trend is for warmer- and drier-than-average weather, meaning drought conditions could worsen before they improve.

articles.title: AFC backs UEFA and CONCACAF who plan boycott over FIFA World Cup proposals
articles.summary: FIFA face global mutiny as Asian Football Confederation stand with Europe and North America after their boycott threats.
articles.titleZh: 亚足联支持欧足联和中北美及加勒比地区足联计划抵制国际足联世界杯提案
articles.summaryZh: 国际足联面临全球叛变，亚足联在欧洲和北美发出抵制威胁后与他们站在一起。

contentParagraphs.en: FIFA face global mutiny as Asian Football Confederation stand with Europe and North America after their boycott threats.The ‌Asian Football Confederation has said it “stands in solidarity” with regional ⁠bodies UEFA and ⁠CONCACAF in opposing plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors but stopped short of threatening ⁠to boycott events run by FIFA, global football’s governing body.The confederation in a statement on Friday expressed “deep concern” over the proposed establishment of a $20bn commercial ⁠subsidiary, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to run the World Cup and FIFA’s other events.Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the FIFA World Cup: All to knowlist 2 of 4What has FIFA charged Argentina with, and what could the punishment be?list 3 of 4Storm apologize after co-owner berates teen girls for support of Cunninghamlist 4 of 4Viral finger-clicker suspended as cricket storm remains in global spotlightend of list“The fact that the situation has reached the point where the real possibility of a FIFA World Cup boycott has entered public discourse should concern everyone ‌who cares about the future of our game,” the statement said.“Football should never have been placed in such a position.”UEFA, European football’s governing body, voted unanimously on Thursday to boycott all FIFA events unless the plans were dropped. CONCACAF, the regional federation for North America, Central America and the Caribbean, has also rejected ⁠FIFA’s proposal.On Thursday, AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa had said the way the proposal had been made was “totally unacceptable”, in a letter to member associations.The AFC said “the proposed FFE cannot realistically achieve the necessary broad consensus and ⁠unity required to move forward.“The FIFA World Cup ⁠is the pinnacle of global football and derives its strength from the participation of all confederations and the world’s leading football nations.”The AFC also made a thinly veiled attack on the ⁠governing body’s president, Gianni Infantino, saying the plan “has exposed fundamental weaknesses in FIFA’s consultation and decision-making processes that ⁠must now be addressed”.Even after FIFA issued ⁠a new statement on Friday, saying each national association “should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future”, the AFC said “central concerns surrounding governance, ‌institutional process and meaningful consultation remain unanswered”.It said the furore must become a catalyst for institutional reform at FIFA, and that “meaningful democracy is not ‌measured ‌solely by the opportunity to vote.“It begins with transparent governance, timely consultation, informed deliberation and genuine participation throughout the decision-making process.”
contentParagraphs.zh: 国际足联面临全球叛变，因为亚洲足球联合会在抵制威胁后与欧洲和北美站在一起。亚洲足球联合会表示，它与地区机构欧足联和中北美洲及加勒比海足球协会“团结一致”，反对向私人投资者出售世界杯股份的计划，但没有威胁抵制全球足球管理机构国际足联举办的赛事。亚洲足球联合会在周五的一份声明中对拟议的设立表示“深切关注”价值 200 亿美元的商业子公司 FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE)，负责运营世界杯和 FIFA 的其他赛事。推荐故事列表 4 项列表 1 of 4 因凡蒂诺计划出售 FIFA 世界杯股份的第 1 项：众所周知列表 2 of 4 国际足联向阿根廷提出了什么指控，以及可能的惩罚是什么？列表 3 of 4 在共同所有者斥责支持 Cunninghamlist 的青少年女孩后，Storm 道歉 4 4 因板球风暴而暂停的病毒式手指点击游戏仍成为全球关注的焦点“事实已经达到了抵制国际足联世界杯的真正可能性已经进入公众讨论的地步，这应该引起所有关心我们足球运动未来的人的关注，”声明称。“足球不应该处于这样的境地。” 欧洲足球管理机构欧足联周四一致投票决定抵制所有国际足联赛事，除非取消计划。北美、中美洲和加勒比地区联合会中北美洲及加勒比海地区联合会也拒绝了国际足联的提议。周四，亚足联主席谢赫·萨勒曼·本·易卜拉欣·阿勒哈利法在致各成员协会的一封信中表示，该提议的提出方式“完全不可接受”。亚足联表示，“提议的FFE实际上无法达成前进所需的广泛共识和团结。”国际足联世界杯是巅峰之作。亚足联还对管理机构主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺进行了毫不掩饰的攻击，称该计划“暴露了国际足联协商和决策过程中的根本弱点，现在必须解决这些弱点”。尽管国际足联周五发表了一份新声明，称每个国家协会“都应该被允许审查该提案并拥有发言权”在塑造自己的未来时”，亚足联表示“围绕治理、制度流程和有意义的协商的核心问题仍未得到解答”。它表示，这种骚动必须成为国际足联制度改革的催化剂，并且“有意义的民主不能仅仅通过投票机会来衡量。“它始于透明的治理、及时的协商、知情的审议和整个决策过程的真正参与。”

articles.title: BP puts North Sea business up for sale
articles.summary: The decision follows a review of BP's operations and is set to end 60 years of production in the region by the oil giant.
articles.titleZh: 英国石油公司 (BP) 出售北海业务
articles.summaryZh: 该决定是在对 BP 的运营进行审查后作出的，该决定将结束这家石油巨头在该地区 60 年的生产。

contentParagraphs.en: BP has said it is putting its North Sea business up for sale in a move that would end 60 years of production in the region by the oil giant.The decision follows a review of BP's operations as it seeks to slim down the group. Its North Sea business has five production hubs - two in the central North Sea and three west of Shetland - and employs about 1,100 people.Earlier this week, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he told US President Donald Trump he would take a "pragmatic approach" to the issue of North Sea oil and gas.Trump, some trade unions, industry figures and some Labour MPs all back increased drilling in the North Sea."The UK has been our home for more than 100 years and will continue to play an important role in our future," BP chief executive Meg O'Neill said."We're proud of the jobs we create, the contribution we make to the UK economy, and the work we do to keep energy flowing every day," she said.The company said it remained committed to operating the business safely and reliably throughout the sale process.Its North Sea business produced 117,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2025, a small fraction of the oil giant's 2.3 million barrels of daily production.The North Sea has increasingly become a topic for political debate.In its 2024 general election manifesto, Labour said it would not issue new licences for drilling, but would honour existing ones.But in recent months, as the Iran war pushed up global oil prices, calls have grown for more North Sea drilling to be approved, from the Conservatives, Reform UK and from President Trump, while also becoming a divisive issue within the Labour party.Some Labour MPs have urged the government to take a more liberal approach, warning that the transition away from oil and gas must protect jobs and the cost of energy bills.But others have backed the government's existing approach, arguing that expanding renewable energy is key to improving energy security and reducing the impact on climate change.As energy secretary in Sir Keir Starmer's government, Ed Miliband was a staunch supporter of the manifesto position. Miliband is now the foreign secretary in Burnham's government.Burnham himself has seemingly left the door open to future drilling. He said he told President Trump this week: "There is a resource there. When people are struggling - you can't ignore that."Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell previously told the BBC that Burnham would stick to the party's manifesto commitments, but there would be a "change of emphasis" on North Sea oil and gas.Oil and gas companies have also criticised the UK's windfall tax, which they argue means the North Sea has lost some of its appeal in recent years.
contentParagraphs.zh: 英国石油公司(BP)表示，将出售其北海业务，此举将结束这家石油巨头在该地区长达60年的生产业务。该决定是在英国石油公司(BP)寻求精简集团业务之际对业务进行审查之后做出的。其北海业务拥有五个生产中心，其中两个位于北海中部，三个位于设得兰群岛西部，拥有约 1,100 名员工。本周早些时候，英国首相安迪·伯纳姆表示，他告诉美国总统唐纳德·特朗普，他将对北海石油和天然气问题采取“务实的态度”。特朗普、一些工会、行业人士和一些工党议员都支持增加在北海的钻探活动。英国石油公司首席执行官梅格·奥尼尔表示：“我们对我们创造的就业机会、对英国经济做出的贡献以及我们为保持能源每天流动所做的工作感到自豪。”该公司表示，在整个销售过程中仍致力于安全可靠地运营业务。2025年，其北海业务每天生产117,000桶油当量，这只是这家石油巨头每天2.3油当量的一小部分。日产量百万桶。北海日益成为政治辩论的话题。工党在2024年大选宣言中表示，不会发放新的钻探许可证，但会尊重现有许可证。但近几个月来，随着伊朗战争推高全球油价，保守党、改革英国和特朗普总统要求批准更多北海钻探的呼声越来越高，同时也成为工党内部的一个分裂问题。一些工党议员敦促政府采取更加自由的态度，警告说，摆脱石油和天然气的转型必须保护就业和能源费用。但其他人支持政府现有的做法，认为扩大可再生能源是改善能源安全和减少对气候变化影响的关键。作为基尔·斯塔默爵士政府的能源部长，埃德·米利班德是宣言立场的坚定支持者。米利班德现在是伯纳姆政府的外交大臣。伯纳姆本人似乎已经为未来的钻探敞开了大门。他说，他本周告诉特朗普总统：“那里有资源。当人们陷入困境时，你不能忽视这一点。”工党副党魁露西·鲍威尔此前告诉英国广播公司，伯纳姆将坚持该党的宣言承诺，但对北海石油和天然气的“重点将发生改变”。石油和天然气公司也批评了英国的暴利税，他们认为这意味着北海近年来失去了一些吸引力。

articles.title: After Fauci Senate hearing, experts worry about 'chilling effect' on public health
articles.summary: The accusations against Dr. Anthony Fauci, once the nation's leading infectious disease expert, have some experts worrying that these events may further erode public health staffing in the U.S.
articles.titleZh: 福奇参议院听证会后，专家担心对公共卫生的“寒蝉效应”
articles.summaryZh: 对曾经的美国顶尖传染病专家安东尼·福奇博士的指控让一些专家担心这些事件可能会进一步削弱美国的公共卫生人员配备。

contentParagraphs.en: Anthony Fauci, former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee hearing in Washington, D.C. Experts worry that the pursuit of Fauci is helping to create a "chilling effect" on public health staffing and infrastructure in the U.S.

contentParagraphs.en: For almost three hours on Wednesday morning, Dr. Anthony Fauci sat before the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and declined to answer questions about the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic.
contentParagraphs.zh: 周三上午，安东尼·福奇博士在参议院国土安全和政府事务委员会坐了近三个小时，拒绝回答有关 COVID-19 大流行起源的问题。

contentParagraphs.en: Instead, he invoked his Fifth Amendment right more than a hundred times — which later led Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., to say he would push to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress next week.
contentParagraphs.zh: 相反，他一百多次援引了第五修正案的权利，这导致肯塔基州共和党参议员兰德·保罗表示，他将在下周推动福奇藐视国会。

contentParagraphs.en: These moves have once again foregrounded Paul's unproven claims that the SARS-Cov-2 virus came from a lab leak and that Fauci covered it up — a charge the scientist has vociferously denied. But the renewed attacks on Fauci, once the nation's leading infectious disease expert, have caused Democrats, health workers and researchers to worry that these events may further erode public health staffing and infrastructure in the U.S.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这些举动再次凸显了保罗未经证实的说法，即 SARS-Cov-2 病毒来自实验室泄漏，而福奇掩盖了这一点，但这位科学家强烈否认了这一指控。但对曾经的美国领先传染病专家福奇的再次攻击让民主党人、卫生工作者和研究人员担心这些事件可能会进一步削弱美国的公共卫生人员和基础设施。

contentParagraphs.en: "These firings and these cuts — they're creating a chilling effect, honestly," Andy Kim, D-N.J., said at the hearing, while also thanking Fauci and decrying what he called the demonization of public servants. "A chilling effect for the next generation of people who might consider stepping up to serve our nation, to be the next generation of researchers who now are wondering whether or not this is the right thing for them to do at a time when they see some of their colleagues, or those that they looked up to, being attacked."
contentParagraphs.zh: 新泽西州民主党人安迪·金 (Andy Kim) 在听证会上表示，“老实说，这些解雇和裁员——它们正在产生寒蝉效应”，同时他还感谢福奇并谴责他所谓的妖魔化公务员。 “这对下一代人来说是一种寒蝉效应，他们可能会考虑站出来为我们的国家服务，成为下一代研究人员，当他们看到自己的一些同事或他们尊敬的人受到攻击时，他们想知道这对他们来说是否是正确的事情。”

contentParagraphs.en: Other public health professionals agree that what played out on Capitol Hill earlier this week is part of a larger corrosion of the field to which they've dedicated their lives, endangering its future and undermining health outcomes in the U.S.
contentParagraphs.zh: 其他公共卫生专业人士一致认为，本周早些时候在国会山发生的事情是对他们毕生致力于的领域更大腐蚀的一部分，危及其未来并损害美国的健康结果。

contentParagraphs.en: "I thought that we were healing as a country around COVID-19," says epidemiologist Katelyn Jetelina. "I think what yesterday did was open some really deep wounds."
contentParagraphs.zh: 流行病学家凯特琳·杰特琳娜 (Katelyn Jetelina) 表示：“我认为，作为一个国家，我们正在从新冠病毒 (COVID-19) 疫情中恢复过来。” “我认为昨天所做的事情打开了一些非常深的伤口。”

contentParagraphs.en: During the pandemic, there was a surge in people asserting their right to reject various medical treatments and public health interventions. It's a movement that's often called health freedom.
contentParagraphs.zh: 疫情期间，主张拒绝各种医疗和公共卫生干预措施的人数激增。这是一场通常被称为健康自由的运动。

contentParagraphs.en: "People were rejecting things like schools demanding that children be vaccinated for COVID before they return to school," says Nicole Huberfeld, a professor of health law at Boston University. But those claims, she says, were not based on empirical evidence. "Rather, they were rooted in often religious or moral objections to vaccination."
contentParagraphs.zh: 波士顿大学健康法教授妮可·胡伯菲尔德 (Nicole Huberfeld) 表示：“人们拒绝学校要求孩子们在返回学校之前接种新冠疫苗等做法。”但她说，这些说法并不是基于经验证据。 “相反，它们往往植根于对疫苗接种的宗教或道德反对。”

contentParagraphs.en: There were other pandemic policies that became increasingly unpopular — masking, social distancing, and school and work closures. People may have accepted these restrictions initially, but "that moment wasn't long-lived in part because there was fairly swift pushback from the top during the first Trump administration," says Huberfeld.
contentParagraphs.zh: 还有其他一些流行病政策变得越来越不受欢迎——戴口罩、保持社交距离以及关闭学校和工作场所。人们最初可能已经接受了这些限制，但“那一刻并没有持续多久，部分原因是在特朗普第一届政府期间，来自高层的抵制相当迅速，”休伯菲尔德说。

contentParagraphs.en: She says interest in 'health freedom' sloped downward during Biden's presidency but it has spiked again during the second Trump administration. "I think it's because people take their signals from the leaders that speak to them," she says. And at this week's hearing, Huberfeld says Republican lawmakers may have been speaking as much to members of their base as they were to Fauci.
contentParagraphs.zh: 她说，在拜登担任总统期间，人们对“健康自由”的兴趣有所下降，但在特朗普第二届政府期间，人们对“健康自由”的兴趣再次飙升。 “我认为这是因为人们从与他们交谈的领导人那里获取了信号，”她说。在本周的听证会上，胡伯菲尔德表示，共和党议员对他们的支持者的讲话可能与对福奇的讲话一样多。

contentParagraphs.en: But in her view, such attacks on the man who once helped lead the federal COVID-19 response, combined with a hollowing out of agencies like the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, add up to a broader assault on the people and programs that keep Americans healthy.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但在她看来，对曾经帮助领导联邦COVID-19应对工作的人的此类攻击，再加上美国卫生与公众服务部等机构的空心化，加起来对维护美国人健康的人和项目造成了更广泛的攻击。

contentParagraphs.en: "I think these hearings play into a larger picture," says Huberfeld, "which is that the field of public health has been devalued significantly by leadership right now. And that devaluing will make it much harder to do the work of public health and it will make it so that the public doesn't trust public health professionals."
contentParagraphs.zh: 胡伯菲尔德说：“我认为这些听证会涉及到一个更大的图景，那就是公共卫生领域目前已被领导层大幅贬值。而这种贬值将使公共卫生工作变得更加困难，并使公众不再信任公共卫生专业人员。”

contentParagraphs.en: Dr. Georges Benjamin, the head of the American Public Health Association, says the consequences of that erosion are already apparent. "We are less healthy," he says. "We've seen it every day, right? This inability to respond effectively to hantavirus, measles, cyclospora."
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国公共卫生协会会长乔治·本杰明博士表示，这种侵蚀的后果已经很明显。 “我们的健康状况较差，”他说。 “我们每天都看到这种情况，对吗？这种无法有效应对汉坦病毒、麻疹、环孢子虫的情况。”

contentParagraphs.en: The results can quickly become dire — especially, states Huberfeld, now that this scenario is compounded by recent sweeping cuts and changes to health care. "I do think there will be more illness and injury, which leads to preventable death," she says.
contentParagraphs.zh: 胡伯菲尔德表示，结果很快就会变得可怕，尤其是最近的医疗保健大幅削减和改革，加剧了这种情况。 “我确实认为将会有更多的疾病和伤害，从而导致可预防的死亡，”她说。

contentParagraphs.en: Problems in the pipeline
contentParagraphs.zh: 管道中的问题

contentParagraphs.en: Benjamin argues that public health professionals need to be able to provide educated and evidence-based information to lawmakers and other officials. But he worries that this week's hearing and the political challenges that Fauci continues to face are likely to be intimidating.
contentParagraphs.zh: 本杰明认为，公共卫生专业人员需要能够向立法者和其他官员提供受过教育且基于证据的信息。但他担心本周的听证会和福奇继续面临的政治挑战可能会令人生畏。

contentParagraphs.en: "If you're going to be threatened by members of Congress, you're going to be a lot less willing to be frank and speak truth to power and give people the information that they desperately need to make decisions," he says. "We can't be tainted by a fear that if we say something, they'll do something to destroy our careers and maybe put our lives at risk."
contentParagraphs.zh: 他说：“如果你受到国会议员的威胁，你就不太愿意坦白向权力说真话，也不太愿意向人们提供他们做出决策时迫切需要的信息。” “我们不能担心，如果我们说了什么，他们就会做一些事情来毁掉我们的职业生涯，甚至可能危及我们的生命。”

contentParagraphs.en: Jetelina, who's also an adjunct professor at the Yale School of Public Health, is concerned about the public health pipeline more broadly. She's witnessed enrollment numbers drop and she's had conversations with her students about their concerns about what a future in the profession might look like.
contentParagraphs.zh: 杰特琳娜也是耶鲁大学公共卫生学院的兼职教授，她对更广泛的公共卫生渠道感到担忧。她目睹了入学人数的下降，并与学生讨论了他们对该行业未来前景的担忧。

contentParagraphs.en: "We're just scientists," she says. "We are never supposed to be on TV and getting croissants thrown at us and death threats. It's a whole new level of risk, and with risk comes really real calculations that people need to make."
contentParagraphs.zh: “我们只是科学家，”她说。 “我们永远不应该在电视上看到向我们扔羊角面包和死亡威胁。这是一个全新的风险水平，伴随着风险，人们需要进行真正的计算。”

articles.title: About 49,000 migrants enter Spanish territory of Ceuta, officials say
articles.summary: The estimated number of arrivals is more than half of the population of the city, which is about 83,600.
articles.titleZh: 官员称，约 49,000 名移民进入西班牙领土休达
articles.summaryZh: 估计抵达人数超过该市人口的一半，即约 83,600 人。

contentParagraphs.en: Figure caption, BySofia Ferreira Santos and Sarah RainsfordSouthern and Eastern Europe correspondentUpdated 33 minutes agoAbout 49,000 migrants have crossed into Spain's North African territory of Ceuta from Morocco in the last 24 hours via land and sea, officials estimate.Videos and images showed thousands of people swimming into the city on Thursday, while local media reported crossings continuing overnight.Officials say at least 18 people have died while trying to reach the territory in recent days.This comes after Spain's Supreme Court ruled this month that migrants stopped at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla, another Spanish exclave, cannot be summarily returned to Morocco.Ceuta, on Morocco's northern coast, is separated from mainland Spain by the Strait of Gibraltar and has long been a focal point for migrants attempting to reach Europe.Local officials had appealed to Madrid for help after a recent rise in attempted crossings, but there were chaotic scenes on Thursday as border controls apparently broke down.The astonishing estimation by Spanish officials suggests the number of migrants who entered into Ceuta in the last day or so could be more than half of the population of the city - which sits at around 83,600, according to the latest local figures.Spain later deployed its armed forces to bolster security in Ceuta and at its sister city of Melilla, where between 300 to 400 crossings were also reported overnight.Coveted by Morocco, both cities have long been a flashpoint in diplomatic relations with Spain. Madrid asserts that both territories are integral parts of Spain and have the same status as the semi-autonomous regions on its mainland.They form the European Union's only land borders with Africa.Image source, ReutersImage caption, Crowds gathered at the border between Morocco and Spain overnightMany of those crossing the border from Morocco have been young, mainly men, although there are also women and children in the crowds and even babies.Officials estimate at least 7,000 of those who crossed illegally into the territory in the last 24 hours are minors.Usually, to try to enter Ceuta, migrants swim several kilometres from further up the coast. This time they appear to have been able to get close to the border fence itself with ease. At the start, some even walked along the rocks on the jetty and around the end of it, but most had to swim out and around to reach the beaches on the other side.It's not clear where the Moroccan border guards were at this point and why the groups of migrants were not dispersed or stopped.Image source, EPA/ShutterstockImage caption, Many young men were seen swimming into Ceuta or crossing the land borderThe sudden influx of people on Thursday followed several days with an increase in arrivals swimming into Ceuta. It appears that word of their success spread quickly.The last time there was a surge in arrivals - though on nowhere near this scale - was in 2021. At that point, the Moroccan authorities allowed some 8,000 people to cross the border following a dispute with Madrid over the sovereignty of the Western Sahara.That diplomatic dispute has flared again recently, after Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez travelled to Algeria which backs independence for the region.Spain's interior ministry said it was working with Morocco to ensure the return of all who crossed illegally into its territory "as soon as possible".Sánchez is set to visit Ceuta later on Friday.Overnight into Friday, crossings continued as did clashes between migrants and police along the border, local media reported.It is not yet clear what prompted this surge in illegal crossings from Morocco, or how hard the authorities there tried to prevent it. At one point, a Spanish official said the border was in total collapse.Italy's prime minister was very quick to comment on events in Ceuta, calling the images from there "shocking" and writing on social media that such "uncontrolled immigration" was a security threat to Europe.She said Italy would consider suspending the Schengen zone agreement with Spain on free movement, although it's unclear what that means in practice given that the two countries are not neighbours and undocumented migrants are unlikely to board flights.In any case, the migrants who have arrived in Ceuta are now stuck there - not on the Spanish mainland.Image source, ReutersImage caption, Spain has now set up a large military presence at the borderHer comments echoed similar remarks made by foreign minister Antonio Tajani, who was accused of weaponising immigration for political ends by his Spanish counterpart, José Manuel Albares.The Spanish foreign minister said such remarks were "improper" for "a partner and friendly country from which we expect European solidarity and not partisan demagoguery".He also summoned the Italian ambassador to Madrid on Friday.The Schengen Area is a system of open borders spanning 29 European countries that have officially abolished controls at their common borders.

articles.titleZh: 人工智能会取代你的工作吗？中国的一些工人已经知道答案
articles.summaryZh:
在全国范围内，在日益脆弱的劳动力市场中，工人们担心人工智能对其生计的影响 
在武汉绿树成荫的街道上，汽车与轻便摩托车和货运卡车争夺空间，最近，一种新型车辆的故障频频发生。

contentParagraphs.en: On the tree-lined streets of Wuhan, where cars jostle for space with mopeds and cargo trucks, the malfunctioning of a new type of vehicle has recently been causing chaos on the city’s roads.In March, several cars from a fleet of driverless taxis stopped abruptly in the streets. The “system malfunction” left distressed riders stranded for hours. The robotaxis, known as Apollo Go and powered by artificial intelligence (AI), were taken off Wuhan’s streets for months for investigations.But the outage was a boon for 45-year-old taxi driver Yao Xinnong. His wages, which had fallen by about 40% since Apollo Go launched in 2022, jumped back up as customers returned.“I don’t really like them, to be honest,” Yao says of the driverless cabs operated by the tech giant Baidu. “Their impact has been huge”.China is encouraging the deployment of AI at a scale unseen in the west. The technology is being rolled out at a staggering rate in an increasingly precarious labour market, and the Wuhan episode helped to highlight the social tensions it is causing.A Baidu driverless robotaxi on the streets of Wuhan in 2024. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty ImagesGig workers like Yao are fearful about the impact of AI on their livelihoods, while recent incidents of white-collar workers being replaced by AI have also sparked a debate over whether workers should embrace the technology – or try to compete with it.Addressing Shanghai’s World AI Conference in July, China’s leader, Xi Jinping, said that AI should be “an important driver for shared prosperity and common security”.But that goal is being pursued amid an increasingly fragile labour market. As well as suffering from high levels of unemployment, China has seen tens of millions of workers drop out of formal employment into the gig economy. According to one thinktank, the number of people in flexible employment will rise to 320 million this year, up from 160 million in 2019. That is about 44% of China’s workforce.China’s gig economyTaxi drivers are one part of this huge cohort. Across the country, as previously heavyweight industries such as real estate and education have floundered, workers have turned to ride-hailing apps to make ends meet. But now the rollout of robotaxis, one of the most popular applications of AI that is already in use in China, is threatening their livelihoods.“If the state really took you into consideration, Apollo Go would never have gone on the market,” says one Wuhan driver.“If things keep going this way in the future, sure, rapid development and scientific progress are great, but ordinary people like us will have no place to survive,” she adds.In 2024, taxi drivers in Wuhan protested against the rollout of Apollo Go in their city. It is unclear how many people took part, because news of the protests were quickly censored. Several drivers interviewed in Wuhan said they had heard about the protests but denied being involved.That year, a Wuhan taxi company, took the rare step of publicly criticising the government’s policy to allow automation on to the city’s streets.“The recent rise of autonomous ride-hailing vehicles has allowed technology to monopolise resources and take away the livelihoods of people at the bottom of society,” the letter said.Taxis wait for fares outside the airport in Wuhan, China. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty ImagesAuthorities in China do not take kindly to public criticism. When the Guardian visited the taxi company’s office in July, an employee declined to be interviewed, citing an agreement with the police to refuse interviews and the risk of detention if he violated the agreement.But two years later, the government is echoing some of the same concerns first voiced by the Wuhan drivers.An editorial published in the state-run Workers’ Daily said that employment rights were “facing new challenges” in the age of AI. contentParagraphs.zh: 武汉绿树成荫的街道上，汽车与轻便摩托车、货运卡车争抢空间，最近，一种新型车辆的故障导致该市道路一片混乱。 今年3月，无人驾驶出租车车队中的几辆车突然停在街道上。 “系统故障”让心疼的乘客滞留了几个小时。这辆名为 Apollo Go 的机器人出租车由人工智能 (AI) 驱动，在武汉街道上停留了数月进行调查。但这次停电对 45 岁出租车司机姚新农来说却是福音。自 2022 年 Apollo Go 推出以来，他的工资下降了约 40%，但随着顾客的回归，他的工资又回升了。“说实话，我不太喜欢它们，”姚在谈到科技巨头百度运营的无人驾驶出租车时说道。 “他们的影响是巨大的”。中国正在鼓励以西方前所未见的规模部署人工智能。在日益不稳定的劳动力市场中，这项技术正在以惊人的速度推出，而武汉的事件凸显了它所造成的社会紧张局势。2024 年，一辆百度无人驾驶机器人出租车出现在武汉街头。照片：彭博社/盖蒂图片社 像姚这样的零工工人担心人工智能对其生计的影响，而最近发生的白领被人工智能取代的事件也引发了一场关于工人是否应该接受这项技术——还是试图与之竞争的争论。在 7 月的上海世界人工智能大会上，中国领导人习近平表示，人工智能应该成为“共同繁荣和共同安全的重要驱动力”。但这一目标是在劳动力市场日益脆弱的情况下实现的。在遭受高失业率的同时，中国还有数以千万计的工人从正规就业岗位转入零工经济。据一家智库预测，今年灵活就业人数将从 2019 年的 1.6 亿增至 3.2 亿，约占中国劳动力的 44%。中国的零工经济出租车司机就是这一庞大群体的一部分。在全国范围内，随着房地产和教育等此前的重量级行业陷入困境，工人们纷纷转向叫车应用来维持收支平衡。但现在，机器人出租车（已经在中国使用的最流行的人工智能应用之一）的推出正在威胁他们的生计。“如果国家真的考虑到你，Apollo Go永远不会上市。”一位武汉司机说道。“如果未来继续这样发展，当然，快速发展和科学进步是伟大的，但像我们这样的普通人将没有生存的地方，”她补充道。2024年，武汉的出租车司机抗议Apollo Go的推出城市。目前尚不清楚有多少人参加，因为抗议活动的消息很快就被审查了。几位在武汉接受采访的司机表示，他们听说了抗议活动，但否认参与其中。当年，武汉一家出租车公司罕见地公开批评政府允许自动化进入城市街道的政策。信中称，“最近自动驾驶网约车的兴起，让技术垄断了资源，夺走了社会底层人民的生计。” 中国武汉机场外，出租车在候车。照片：Bloomberg/Getty Images 中国当局并不善待公众的批评。当《卫报》7月份拜访出租车公司办公室时，一名员工拒绝接受采访，理由是与警方达成协议，拒绝采访，如果违反协议，就有被拘留的风险。但两年后，政府回应了武汉司机最初表达的一些同样的担忧。国营《工人日报》发表社论称，在人工智能时代，就业权利“面临新挑战”。文章警告“传统就业规则与人工智能技术迭代之间的碰撞”。政府最近承诺“全面应对外部环境变化和人工智能等新技术发展对就业的影响”。中国科技分析师徐琳娜表示，北京方面出现了“重大氛围转变”。她表示，去年本土人工智能模式DeepSeek取得成功后，中国“非常支持人工智能发展”。“今年，如果你看看某些新的指导方针，徐说：“人们更加重视人工智能促进就业和以人为本的做法。”北京中关村高新区政府官员程万辉表示，当局正在“密切关注人工智能带来的社会问题，以及潜在的道德问题。”“关键是每个人都要转变观念，将人工智能视为一种工具，并学会如何将其应用到未来的工作中。”最近的法院判决已对被公司解雇的白领将被人工智能取代。但许多工人担心人工智能的普及将成为他们获得工作的障碍。 田泽民是一名在北京工作的电影摄影师，在电影行业工作了近二十年。但现在他失业了。他在一篇关于人工智能的社交媒体帖子中写道：“我花了六年的时间努力成为一名电影摄影师，结果被一个软件所取代。”他告诉《卫报》，“我以为我会在这个行业度过一生。但人工智能的出现让我第一次感到巨大的震惊。”随着人工智能在电影行业得到更广泛的采用，田的许多同行都在失败。他自己作为自由职业者的比例现在是 2019 年的 40%。田说，他对人工智能的进步感到震惊。去年，它制作了一些笨拙、长相怪异的化身。现在，它可以制作令人信服的数字克隆，其范围可以携带一部长片。田说：“我们几乎没有时间做出反应。”许多分析人士认为，中国政府

articles.title: Thames Water boss says leakage targets 'not realistic'
articles.summary: Chris Weston said Thames wanted "to do better" but some of its targets were not achievable.
articles.titleZh: 泰晤士水务公司老板表示泄漏目标“不现实”
articles.summaryZh: 克里斯·韦斯顿表示，泰晤士河希望“做得更好”，但其中一些目标无法实现。

contentParagraphs.en: Water companies have performance commitments on issues such as leakage. It is illegal to release raw sewage into rivers and seas during "normal" weather conditions, but firms are allowed to do so when it rains heavily, to prevent homes being flooded.Thames is the UK's largest water company, supplying water and wastewater services to 16 million customers across London and parts of southern England.Speaking to the BBC's Big Boss Interview podcast, Weston said the company treats 4.3 billion litres of waste a day, and "99.5% of the time" it gets treated successfully, although "sometimes something goes wrong"."We want to do better when it comes to pollutions," he said, but added, "the targets that the company is expected to make are not realistic."[For example], we have to hit a certain level of leakage, but it is so far in excess of what we are capable of doing, I think anyone would be capable of doing, however much money you invested, that it is not going to be achievable."The chance of getting to zero pollution was "very, very slim", he added.Ofwat told the BBC: "With around a fifth of water put into supply still lost through leakage, companies must deliver on the commitments they have been funded to achieve."Water company targets are intended to be ambitious and drive better outcomes for customers and the environment."A spokesperson for the Environment Agency said: "[We] and the public expect Thames Water to comply with the law," adding that the agency would continue to hold companies to account where performance falls short.James Wallace, chief executive of campaign group River Action, said: "Thames Water's tactics of opacity and deflection fool no-one. Telling the public to save water while this wasteful profit-obsessed corporation leaks 570 million litres of treated drinking water every day is offensive. "There is nothing 'realistic' about accepting sewage pollution as inevitable. The choice is simple: keep propping up a failed privatised financial model, or put Thames Water into special administration and rebuild it as a public utility serving customers, rivers and the public."
contentParagraphs.zh: 自来水公司对渗漏等问题有绩效承诺。在“正常”天气条件下，将未经处理的污水排入河流和海洋是违法的，但在大雨时，公司可以这样做，以防止房屋被洪水淹没。泰晤士报业是英国最大的自来水公司，为伦敦和英格兰南部部分地区的 1600 万客户提供供水和废水处理服务。韦斯顿在接受 BBC 的 Big Boss Interview 播客时表示，该公司每天处理 43 亿升废物，“99.5% 的废物” “我们希望在污染方面做得更好，”他说，但又补充道，“公司预期制定的目标并不现实。”[例如]，我们必须达到一定程度的泄漏，但这远远超出了我们的能力范围，我认为任何人都有能力做到，无论你投入多少钱，这都是不可能实现的。“实现零污染的机会是他补充说，“非常非常渺茫”。 Ofwat 告诉 BBC：“大约五分之一的供水仍然因泄漏而损失，公司必须兑现他们已获得资金实现的承诺。”水务公司的目标旨在雄心勃勃，为客户和环境带来更好的结果。“环境署发言人表示：“[我们]和公众期望泰晤士水务局遵守法律，”并补充说，该机构将继续追究绩效不佳的公司的责任。该活动首席执行官詹姆斯·华莱士河流行动组织表示：“泰晤士水务公司的不透明和偏转策略骗不了任何人。告诉公众节约用水，而这家浪费性的、痴迷于利润的公司每天泄漏 5.7 亿升经过处理的饮用水，这是令人反感的。”接受污水污染不可避免是不现实的。选择很简单：继续支撑失败的私有化金融模式，或者将泰晤士水务纳入特殊管理，并将其重建为服务客户、河流和公众的公用事业。”

articles.title: Danube's record low levels force shutdown of Hungary's only nuclear plant
articles.summary: Romania, Bulgaria and Serbia are also grappling with the effects of a series of prolonged heatwaves and low rainfall.
articles.titleZh: 多瑙河创纪录的低水位迫使匈牙利唯一的核电站关闭
articles.summaryZh: 罗马尼亚、保加利亚和塞尔维亚也正在应对一系列长期热浪和低降雨量的影响。

contentParagraphs.en: Image source, EPAImage caption, The level of the water of the Danube is so low that the nuclear power plant's suction nozzles cannot reach itByLaura Gozzi and Paul KirbyEurope digital editorHungary's only nuclear power plant will be forced to shut down entirely for the first time due to record low water levels of the River Danube, Prime Minister Péter Magyar has said.The Soviet-era Paks power plant uses the Danube for cooling but the water level is so low that the suction nozzles cannot reach it. Magyar warned Hungary's energy supply could become "critical" from Monday due to the Paks shutdown and the ongoing heatwave, which will see temperatures hover around 37C for a week.Like much of Europe, Hungary has seen very low rainfall and high temperatures for much of the summer.The waters of the Danube have fallen to the lowest levels for 30 years in several countries, including neighbouring Serbia and Romania.Magyar asked Hungarians to limit activities that required significant energy consumption between the peak times of 17:00 and 22:00, including charging electric cars and using air conditioning equipment.A "rotational shutdown regime" was also possible if the other combined efforts were not enough to maintain the balance of the national grid, Magyar said, adding the government would compile a list of electricity and water consumers whose consumption could be limited.Image source, Anadolu via Getty ImagesImage caption, Large areas of the riverbed have been exposed in the centre of Budapest after weeks of extreme heat and droughtIn Romania, one of the country's only two nuclear reactors has been shut down at the Cernavoda power plant, which provides about 20% of the country's power.The first of the two 706-megawatt reactors was shut down earlier this week because the Danube's levels were so low, and state-owned company Nuclearelectrica was trying to avoid closing down the other on Thursday. If the second reactor is shut down Romania will, like Hungary, be temporarily without any nuclear energy production.Climate change is driving up temperatures around the world - but particularly in Europe.It is the fasting warming continent, heating up twice as fast as the global average, according to the Copernicus climate service. This is causing increased summer heatwaves, greater pressure on Europe's waters and more intense wildfires. Image source, ReutersImage caption, Among the wrecks exposed by the low levels of the Danube was a World War Two German warship at Prahovo in SerbiaRomania's National Institute of Hydrology says the average river flow where the Danube enters the country is 4,700 cubic metres per second in July, whereas on Wednesday it was down to less than a third of that, at 1,600cm per second. The institute forecast it would continue to fall to 1,500cm per second by Tuesday.The Danube runs 2,857km (1,775 miles) through 19 countries.The Upper Danube goes from Germany to the Slovak capital Bratislava, the middle basin runs from Bratislava to the border between Serbia and Romania and the Lower Danube extends through Romania and Bulgaria into the three main branches of the Danube Delta that flow into the Black Sea.The low waters of the river have resulted in several unexpected discoveries. The remains of a sunken Hungarian cargo ship resurfaced in Croatia, while the hulks of a German river flotilla was seen in Serbia. And a resident of the northeastern Bulgarian city of Ruse found bones on the Danube river bed, which experts determined were the remains of a mammoth. They were able to recognise a lower jaw, two tusks, and possibly a mammoth rib.Image source, Inquam Photos/Ovidiu Micsik/ReutersImage caption, River flow in Serbia on the Danube is now a third of the average for JulyShipping has ground to a halt on the river in Bulgaria, and border police had to evacuate 186 river cruise passengers from the Viking Ullur ship earlier this week when it ran aground close to Vidin, a city that sits on the border with Romania. Passengers had been running low on food and water because the cruise ship was unable to dock in Vidin, and another boat that was called in to help was unable to get close enough."I have never heard of such low levels over the years. There has certainly not been a similar situation since 1990," Ivan Zhekov, head of river supervision at Bulgaria's maritime administration agency told BTA news agency.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Boats lie on the dried-out Danube riverbed in front of the Calafat-Vidin bridge, connecting Bulgaria and RomaniaIt is not just the Danube where river levels are low. In Serbia, the levels are also very low on the Sava and Tisa, which are both tributaries of the Danube.Serbian hydrologist Dejan Vladiković said the problems were not just down to the current high temperatures but also to low rainfall during the spring. He told Serbian TV channel N1 that the Danube was down to levels not seen for 50 to 60 years, and climatologists did not expect to see any improvement until mid-September.Temperatures in Serbia are set to climb as high as 38C on Friday, and locally up to 40C, with night-time temperatures in Belgrade as high as 26C.Elsewhere in Europe, forecasters say fire-prone conditions are expected to spread towards central Europe, with Greece and Turkey among the countries worst affected. Vast areas of France and Spain have just experienced some of the most intense and widespread wildfires in living memory, leading to hundreds of thousands of evacuations.

contentParagraphs.en: Pressure is growing on FIFA and its president Gianni Infantino following proposals for private investment in World Cups.Carlos Cordeiro, senior adviser to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, has resigned following the proposal by football’s governing body to sell a stake in its World Cups and events.Cordeiro said on Friday that he is stepping down with immediate effect in ⁠protest at proposals to seek private investment in a newly formed FIFA Forward Enterprise venture, ‌calling the plan “a bad deal for football”.Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the FIFA World Cup: All to knowlist 2 of 4What has FIFA charged Argentina with, and what could the punishment be?list 3 of 4Storm apologize after co-owner berates teen girls for support of Cunninghamlist 4 of 4Viral finger-clicker suspended as cricket storm remains in global spotlightend of listIn FIFA’s plan, the FFE would create a $20bn subsidiary to run the World Cup and its other events, with a stake of up to 20 percent to be offered to external investors.“Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal ⁠and I oppose ⁠it unequivocally,” Cordeiro said in a statement.“It is ⁠a bad deal for ⁠FIFA’s Member Associations, ⁠a bad deal for football and a bad deal ‌for the long-term future of the game.”Cordeiro had represented football’s global governing body on the White House Task Force for the 2026 World Cup, held in the United States, Canada and Mexico.A former banker and ex-US Soccer Federation vice president, Cordeiro was hand-picked to ⁠help grow world football for FIFA.In his statement, Cordeiro questioned why FIFA would consider raising $4.2bn by selling part of its “most valuable asset” when the organisation sits on billions of dollars in reserves and has no debt.His resignation comes as FIFA’s 211 member associations face pressure to decide on the controversial proposal by September 19, with Cordeiro ⁠saying they “risk being left behind” if they do not accept it.“The ⁠FIFA President himself has highlighted the $15bn in revenue generated between 2022 and 2026,” Cordeiro added, saying FIFA already had the financial capacity to provide additional support to member associations from its existing resources.“Against that backdrop, selling ⁠a permanent stake in football’s most valuable asset to raise $4.2bn makes little sense.”As senior adviser to Infantino, Cordeiro’s remit ⁠was to “advise FIFA on new strategic initiatives to grow the ⁠game at all levels”.Announcing the appointment in 2021, Infantino had said: “Carlos is the right person to advise us as we modernise our regulatory framework and grow the sport in ways that advance football for men, women and youth ‌across the globe.”Cordeiro built a long career in business and global investment banking in Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) and across Asia, advising governments and some of the world’s ‌largest ‌international companies.Prior to joining US Soccer, he was a vice chairman at Goldman Sachs and earned an MBA from Harvard Business School.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在提议对世界杯进行私人投资后，国际足联及其主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺面临的压力越来越大。国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺的高级顾问卡洛斯·科代罗在足球管理机构提议出售其世界杯和赛事的股份后辞职。科代罗周五表示，他将立即辞职，以抗议寻求私人投资新成立的国际足联前锋企业合资企业的提议，称该计划“对足球来说是一笔糟糕的交易”。列表 4 项列表 1（共 4）因凡蒂诺计划出售 FIFA 世界杯股份：全部了解列表 2（共 4）国际足联对阿根廷提出了什么指控，以及可能的处罚是什么？列表 3（共 4）风暴在共同所有者斥责青少年女孩支持坎宁安后道歉列表 4（共 4）由于板球风暴仍然受到全球关注，病毒手指点击游戏被暂停列表末尾在国际足联的计划中，FFE 将创建一个价值 200 亿美元的子公司，负责运营世界杯及其他赛事，并向外部投资者提供高达 20% 的股份。“让我明确一点：我没有参与这项提议，而且我明确反对它，”科代罗在一份声明中表示。“这对国际足联会员协会来说是一笔糟糕的交易，对足球来说是一笔糟糕的交易，对这项运动的长远未来来说也是一笔糟糕的交易。”科代罗是负责 2026 年在美国、加拿大和墨西哥举行的世界杯的白宫工作组的全球足球管理机构。科代罗曾是银行家和前美国足协副主席，他被精心挑选来帮助国际足联发展世界足球。科代罗在声明中质疑，当国际足联拥有数十亿美元的储备金且没有债务时，为什么国际足联会考虑通过出售部分“最有价值的资产”来筹集 42 亿美元。国际足联的 211 个会员协会面临着在 9 月 19 日之前就这一有争议的提议做出决定的压力，科代罗表示，如果不接受该提议，他们“就有被抛在后面的风险”。“国际足联主席本人强调了 2022 年至 2026 年间产生的 150 亿美元的收入，”科代罗补充道，并表示国际足联已经有财务能力利用其现有资源向会员协会提供额外支持。足球最有价值的资产筹集 42 亿美元毫无意义。”作为因凡蒂诺的高级顾问，科代罗的职责是“就新的战略举措向国际足联提供建议，以在各个层面发展这项运动”。因凡蒂诺在 2021 年宣布这一任命时表示：“卡洛斯是为我们提供建议的合适人选，我们将推动监管框架现代化，并以促进全世界男女和青少年足球发展的方式发展这项运动。 Cordeiro 在欧洲、中东和非洲 (EMEA) 以及整个亚洲的商业和全球投资银行领域拥有长期的职业生涯，为政府和一些世界上最大的国际公司提供咨询。在加入美国足球之前，他曾担任高盛副主席，并获得了哈佛商学院的 MBA 学位。

articles.title: Amazon and Apple just told us more about their AI plans - here are three things we learned
articles.summary: Billions of dollars are being poured into a new wave of AI technology. But will it pay off?
articles.titleZh: 亚马逊和苹果刚刚告诉我们更多有关他们的人工智能计划的信息 - 以下是我们了解到的三件事
articles.summaryZh: 数十亿美元正在投入新一波的人工智能技术。但它会得到回报吗？

contentParagraphs.en: OpenAI's release of ChatGPT in late 2022 kicked off the ongoing AI investment race, and every major tech company has since launched a consumer-facing AI chatbot of their own. Meta has Meta AI, Google has Gemini. Amazon has Rufus. Apple even relaunched Siri.Yet, none of the chatbots or the related tools in and of themselves clearly provide a meaningful amount of revenue for the companies, despite being costly to create.Instead, this batch of earnings results made clear that companies like Google, which is owned by Alphabet, and Meta are currently spending much more money related to AI tools than they bring in.Both companies reported some of their lowest ever amounts of free cash flow, a measure of how much money a business has left over after paying for operations and investments.Google spent so much money on AI that Alphabet's free cash flow was negative on revenue of $118bn, meaning it spent more than it brought in for the first time in the company's history as a public company.Meta's free cash was just $784m on $61bn of revenue, meaning it spent almost as much money as it made during the quarter.Meta's Reality Labs, which is responsible for its AI work, lost nearly $9bn in the first half of this year.Look no further than Wall Street's reaction to Meta's quarterly results to see that investors are no longer placated with executive's claims that AI investment will turn out to be worth it at some unknown point in the future.Shares of the social media giant plunged to its second lowest level in a year after chief executive Mark Zuckerberg said Meta was working on its own AI agent, or an AI chatbot that can operate somewhat autonomously. And that it was planning to develop an operation to sell an an AI tool directly to other firms.Neither the operation or the AI tool currently exist in a way that could make Meta money, and Zuckerberg gave no timeline for when they would materialise. Still, Meta increased the low end of its planned spending on AI – it is likely to pour more than $140bn into AI this year alone.Meanwhile, shares in Microsoft soared to a six-month high. Despite the company's plans to effectively match this financial year the $190bn it spent on AI over the last 12 months, it showed strong revenue growth and more adoption of its core AI tool.Tracy Woo, an analyst with Forrester, said Microsoft was a tech company showing that its massive AI investments were "beginning to deliver returns."The market reaction to Amazon was almost identical. Despite negative cash flow, and plans to spend $220bn on AI this year, the success of its other businesses drove its stock to its highest price in two months.AI tools may have not yet proven to be a consumer tech revolution on the scale of the internet or even electricity, external, as many tech executives have promised for years. But there is still huge demand from people for new technology.Google said last week that 950 million people are using its Gemini chatbot at least once a month, three times the users it had a year ago.Apple on Thursday said that new versions of its core products, the Mac computer, iPhone and iPad, have been selling better this year than the company planned for or expected.So much so that it warned investors, external that sales of such products would slow down, because Apple is unable to get enough of the microchips that would be required to meet buyer demand.The company is, however, anticipating a lot of excitement from Apple users for its impending update of Siri, its AI voice assistant within its products that is getting an overhaul with the help of Google's Gemini chatbot.Outgoing chief executive Tim Cook said Apple already has plans to charge users who wish to make heavier use of the new Siri, given feedback received from user testing so far."We're off-the-charts excited about Siri AI", Cook said. "We do believe there will be people who want to use it – a lot."
contentParagraphs.zh: OpenAI 在 2022 年底发布的 ChatGPT 拉开了正在进行的人工智能投资竞赛的序幕，此后各大科技公司都推出了自己的面向消费者的人工智能聊天机器人。 Meta 有 Meta AI，Google 有 Gemini。亚马逊有鲁弗斯。苹果甚至重新推出了 Siri。然而，尽管创建成本高昂，但聊天机器人或相关工具本身并没有明显为公司提供有意义的收入。相反，这批财报结果清楚地表明，Alphabet 旗下的谷歌和 Meta 等公司目前在人工智能工具方面的支出远多于其带来的收入。两家公司都报告了有史以来最低的自由现金流量，这是衡量企业在支付运营和投资后剩余多少钱的指标。在 AI 上投入的资金如此之多，以至于 Alphabet 的自由现金流为负值，收入为 1180 亿美元，这意味着它作为上市公司历史上首次支出超过收入。Meta 的自由现金仅为 7.84 亿美元，收入为 610 亿美元，这意味着它在本季度的支出几乎与它在本季度赚到的钱一样多。负责 AI 工作的 Meta 的 Reality Labs 今年上半年亏损了近 90 亿美元。看看华尔街的情况就知道了。人们对 Meta 季度业绩的反应表明，投资者不再满足于高管声称人工智能投资将在未来某个未知时刻变得值得的说法。在首席执行官马克·扎克伯格表示 Meta 正在开发自己的人工智能代理或可以某种程度上自主运行的人工智能聊天机器人后，这家社交媒体巨头的股价跌至一年来的第二低水平。该公司还计划开发一项业务，直接向其他公司出售人工智能工具。目前该业务或人工智能工具都无法以可以为 Meta 赚钱的方式存在，扎克伯格也没有给出具体实现的时间表。尽管如此，Meta 仍提高了其人工智能计划支出的下限——仅今年就可能向人工智能投入超过 1400 亿美元。 与此同时，微软的股价飙升至六个月高点。尽管该公司计划在本财年有效匹配过去 12 个月在人工智能上花费的 1900 亿美元，但它显示出强劲的收入增长和对其核心人工智能工具的更多采用。Forrester 分析师 Tracy Woo 表示，微软是一家科技公司，表明其大规模的人工智能投资“开始带来回报”。市场对亚马逊的反应几乎相同。尽管现金流为负，并计划今年在人工智能上投入 2200 亿美元，但其他业务的成功将其股价推至两个月来的最高水平。人工智能工具可能尚未被证明是一场互联网甚至电力、外部规模的消费者技术革命，正如许多科技高管多年来所承诺的那样。但人们对新技术的需求仍然巨大。谷歌上周表示，每月至少有 9.5 亿人使用其 Gemini 聊天机器人，是一年前用户数量的三倍。苹果周四表示，其核心产品新版本 Mac 电脑、iPhone 和 iPad 今年的销量比该公司计划或预期的要好。以至于它向外界警告投资者，此类产品的销售将会放缓，因为苹果无法获得满足买家所需的足够微芯片。然而，该公司预计苹果用户会对即将推出的 Siri 更新感到兴奋，Siri 是其产品中的人工智能语音助手，在谷歌 Gemini 聊天机器人的帮助下正在进行彻底改革。即将卸任的首席执行官蒂姆·库克表示，鉴于迄今为止收到的用户测试反馈，苹果已经计划向那些希望更多地使用新 Siri 的用户收费。库克表示，“我们对 Siri AI 感到非常兴奋”。 “我们确实相信会有很多人想要使用它。”

articles.title: 'I pay £580 a month to live in a disused care home': Property guardians show us around
articles.summary: Could you live communally in a disused building in exchange for a heavily discounted rent? Property guardians show us around.
articles.titleZh: “我每月支付 580 英镑住在废弃的护理院”：财产监护人带我们参观
articles.summaryZh: 你能住在一栋废弃的建筑里，以换取大幅折扣的租金吗？财产监护人带我们四处参观。

contentParagraphs.en: Image source, Moses KamangaImage caption, Katrina has been living in a former care home for 10 monthsByDaniel ThomasBusiness reporterWould you live in a disused care home, pub or bank in exchange for a heavily discounted rent? As cost of living pressures persist, a growing number of people are applying to become so-called property guardians - living in vacant residential or commercial buildings to protect them from squatters, vandalism and disrepair.They typically pay 30-50% less rent than private tenants, sometimes with bills thrown in, in exchange for looking after the buildings.However property guardians also have significantly fewer rights than private renters and can be evicted with just 28 days' notice.Katrina, 29, has spent the last 10 months living with around 50 other people in an Edwardian mansion in Hampstead, London, which was used as a care home until 2015.Image source, KatrinaImage caption, One of the communal living areas in Katrina's 50-person house shareThe postgraduate student, who says she could not afford to rent privately in the capital, currently pays £580 a month for her room including bills and council tax, about £400 below the London average, external. Katrina says guardianship gives her the chance to live in an unusual property and describes the mansion as an "incredible" and "romantic" place despite it being "quite run down". Set in 1.7 acres of gardens, the building has grand staircases, south-west-facing balconies and chandeliers in some rooms, but it does have some downsides: "We've had mushrooms growing on the walls, leaks, parts of the balcony stonework have fallen off," says Katrina.Image source, LOWEImage caption, The disused care home has high ceilings and large windowsKatrina says she loves the communal aspect of guardianship, which is "somewhere between living in university halls, a block of flats and a fancy squat".She lives with "all sorts of people", from lawyers to artists, sharing bathrooms, a kitchen and communal living areas, and regularly socialising.But there are disagreements over things like noise, she says. And while Lowe, the company that manages the property, operates a stringent vetting process for its guardians, two residents have been asked to leave because of antisocial behaviour - one for alleged sexual harassment. Lowe tells the BBC it acts "quickly and decisively" on the rare occasion someone breaches its standards and that the "overwhelming majority" of guardians go on to be "brilliant, community-minded residents".'It's really precarious'In general, guardians have fewer rights than private renters, external because they hold a "licence to occupy" rather than a tenancy. Guardianship companies are not obliged to protect their deposits or carry out repairs not specifically provided for in the agreement. Landlords can also visit at any time, without warning, and evict residents without giving a reason. Katrina admits she worries about the temporary nature of her arrangement sometimes. A developer bought the former care home last year and plans to turn it into flats, so she will eventually have to leave. "It's really precarious in that sense. It's not guaranteed to last. If anyone doesn't like that, it's not for them," she says.Image source, David HaleImage caption, David Hale has lived in a disused school in South London for the last three yearsLast year, the Property Guardian Providers Association (PGPA) estimated there were between 10,000 and 15,000 property guardians in the UK, mainly in major cities, with most aged between 20 and 35.The trade group says the number of people applying has risen sharply as rental costs soar. David Hale, 32, became a guardian almost 10 years ago to save money and has never lived in standard rental accommodation.He and his wife now rent a "massive" space at a former primary school in Brixton, South London, for around £1,500 a month, including bills and council tax. He says they wouldn't be able to afford a similar property otherwise and save about £1,000 a month. Tips on becoming a property guardianPrepare to be flexible: You may stay for several years, or you may need to move on with relatively short notice.Choose an established guardian company: Look for a reputable provider with good health and safety proceduresRead your licence agreement carefully: Understand your responsibilities to the building, house rules and visitor policies Know your rights: Guardians are legally entitled to a court order before they can be evicted and their home must be safe to live inEmbrace community living: Be considerate of those you live with and respect shared areas.Sources: the Property Guardian Providers Association, Shelter, Ad Hoc Property ManagementImage source, David HaleImage caption, Large open classrooms have been converted into living spaceAround 20 guardians live in the school's open classrooms and offices, sharing a kitchen and large garden. But while David has enjoyed communal living, he and his wife are saving to buy their own home: "We wouldn't want to share toilets and bathrooms forever. We also want to start a family." The PGPA believes guardianship could help ease the UK's housing crisis by providing affordable temporary accommodation for thousands of people. It points out that over a million homes currently stand empty, along with tens of millions of square feet, external of non-residential property.But housing charity Shelter argues the rise of property guardianship shows how people are being forced "further and further afield just to keep a roof over their heads"."For most, this isn't a good alternative to an affordable, stable home," says chief executive Sarah Elliott.
