contentParagraphs.zh: 图片来源，Moses Kamanga 图片说明，卡特里娜飓风已经在以前的疗养院里生活了 10 个月 作者：丹尼尔·托马斯 商业记者 你愿意住在废弃的疗养院、酒吧或银行中以换取大幅折扣的租金吗？随着生活成本压力持续存在，越来越多的人正在申请成为所谓的财产监护人 - 居住在空置的住宅或商业建筑中，以保护他们免受擅自占地、破坏和年久失修的侵害。他们通常比私人租户少支付 30-50% 的租金，有时还需要缴纳账单，以换取照看建筑物的费用。然而，财产监护人的权利也比私人租户少得多，只需提前 28 天通知即可被驱逐。卡特里娜， 29 岁的她在过去 10 个月里与大约 50 个人一起住在伦敦汉普斯特德的一栋爱德华七世时代的宅邸中，该宅邸在 2015 年之前一直被用作疗养院。 图片来源，Katrina 图片说明，Katrina 的 50 人房屋中的一个公共生活区这位研究生说，她负担不起在首都的私人租金，目前每月为她的房间支付 580 英镑，包括账单和市政税，大约比伦敦外部平均水平低 400 英镑。卡特里娜表示，监护权让她有机会住在一处不寻常的房产中，并形容这座豪宅是一个“令人难以置信”和“浪漫”的地方，尽管它“相当破旧”。这座建筑坐落在占地 1.7 英亩的花园中，拥有宏伟的楼梯、朝西南的阳台，部分房间还配有枝形吊灯，但它确实有一些缺点：“我们的墙壁上长出了蘑菇，漏水，部分阳台的石雕已经脱落，”卡特里娜说。她和“各种各样的人”住在一起，从律师到艺术家，共用浴室、厨房和公共生活区，并定期进行社交活动。但她说，在噪音等问题上存在分歧。虽然管理该物业的 Lowe 公司对其监护人实行严格的审查程序，但两名居民因反社会行为而被要求离开，其中一名居民涉嫌性骚扰。洛告诉英国广播公司，在极少数情况下有人违反其标准，他们会“迅速而果断”地采取行动，而且“绝大多数”监护人都是“才华横溢、有社区意识的居民”。“这真的很不稳定”。一般来说，监护人的权利比私人租房者少，因为他们持有“占用许可证”而不是租约。监护公司没有义务保护其押金或进行协议中未明确规定的维修。房东还可以在没有警告的情况下随时登门拜访，并在不给出理由的情况下驱逐居民。卡特里娜承认，她有时会担心自己的安排是暂时的。一位开发商去年买下了这栋前疗养院，并计划将其改造成公寓，所以她最终不得不离开。她说：“从这个意义上来说，这真的很不稳定。它不能保证持续下去。如果有人不喜欢这样，那就不适合他们。” 图片来源，大卫·黑尔 图片说明，大卫·黑尔过去三年一直住在伦敦南部一所废弃的学校。去年，财产监护人提供者协会 (PGPA) 估计，英国有 10,000 到 15,000 名财产监护人，主要分布在大城市，其中大多数年龄在 10,000 到 15,000 名财产监护人之间。 20和35.该行业组织表示，随着租金成本飙升，申请人数急剧增加。 32 岁的戴维·黑尔 (David Hale) 大约 10 年前为了省钱而成为一名监护人，从未住过标准的出租房。他和妻子现在在伦敦南部布里克斯顿的一所前小学租了一个“巨大”的空间，每月租金约为 1,500 英镑，包括账单和市政税。他说，否则他们就买不起类似的房产，每月可以节省约 1,000 英镑。成为财产监护人的建议 准备灵活：您可能会停留数年，或者可能需要在相对较短的时间内搬走。选择一家成熟的监护人公司：寻找具有良好健康和安全程序的信誉良好的提供商 仔细阅读您的许可协议：了解您对建筑物的责任、房屋规则和访客政策 了解您的权利：监护人在被驱逐之前依法有权获得法院命令，并且他们的房屋必须安全居住 拥抱社区生活：体谅与您同住的人并尊重共同的人资料来源：财产监护人提供者协会、Shelter、Ad Hoc Property Management 图片来源、David Hale 图片说明，大型开放式教室已改造成居住空间 大约 20 名监护人住在学校的开放式教室和办公室里，共用厨房和大花园。尽管大卫享受公共生活，但他和妻子正在攒钱买自己的房子：“我们不想永远共用厕所和浴室。我们也想组建一个家庭。” PGPA 认为，监护权可以为数千人提供负担得起的临时住宿，从而有助于缓解英国的住房危机。报告指出，目前有超过一百万套房屋空置，还有数千万平方英尺的非住宅物业。但住房慈善机构 Shelter 认为，财产监护权的兴起表明，人们被迫“越来越远，只是为了有一个栖身之所”。“对于大多数人来说，这并不是一个负担得起的、稳定的住房的好替代方案，”首席执行官莎拉·埃利奥特 (Sarah Elliott) 说。联系您是否受到本报道中涉及的问题的影响？获取我们的旗舰新闻通讯，其中包含您开始新的一天所需的所有头条新闻。在这里注册。

articles.title: Hosepipe bans in force as drought declared - is your area affected?
articles.summary: More than 20 million households have been placed under hosepipe bans due to higher demand and low rainfall.
articles.titleZh: 宣布干旱后，软管禁令生效 - 您所在的地区受到影响了吗？
articles.summaryZh: 由于需求增加和降雨量减少，超过 2000 万户家庭被禁止使用软管。

contentParagraphs.en: Hosepipe bans in force as drought declared - is your area affected?Image source, Matt Cardy/Getty ImagesByMark PoyntingClimate reporterJess CarrData designer and Phil LeakeData journalistUpdated 30 July 2026Drought has been declared across large parts of England and the whole of Wales as successive heatwaves have left water supplies under strain.The Environment Agency (EA) has announced that more than half of England is now in drought, with central, eastern and southern areas most affected.A drought now also covers all of Wales, after Natural Resources Wales (NRW) extended the measure initially brought in for North Wales and the Upper Severn river basin.Both England and Wales are on course to record the driest July on record, which - on top of hot, dry conditions in spring and early summer and increased demand - has left water supplies heavily depleted.More than 20 million people in England and Wales have now been placed under a hosepipe ban. This means hosepipes cannot be used for watering gardens, washing vehicles and windows and filling pools.So how is your area doing and are you in a drought?There is no single definition of drought, but it often begins with a period of low rainfall. As the ground dries out, crops and vegetation can begin to struggle. If dry conditions persist, rivers, reservoirs and groundwater levels can also fall, putting pressure on water supplies.Environmental bodies in each UK nation decide whether to declare drought or water scarcity by assessing current water resources alongside weather forecasts.Both drought and water scarcity can lead to hosepipe bans. While drought is driven by prolonged dry weather, water scarcity occurs when demand for water outstrips the available supply. This summer, restrictions have been introduced in some areas to help manage high demand.But while recent months have seen temperatures regularly exceed 30C, winter was much wetter than usual.It has raised questions about how effectively water resources are being managed, and whether the UK is prepared for drier summers expected with climate change.Half of England and all of Wales in droughtSo far, eight UK water companies have announced hosepipe bans - seven are spread across central, southern and eastern parts of England, and one is in Wales.In England, more than half of the country is now in drought. The areas affected are East Anglia, Hertfordshire and the whole of London, Thames Valley, Hampshire and the Isle of Wight, Devon and Cornwall, the West Midlands, and Wessex (covering Dorset, Somerset, Wiltshire, and South Gloucestershire).Several other areas of England are in "prolonged dry weather" - the category below drought - while only Yorkshire and the North East remain in "normal" status.Elsewhere, the whole of Wales is in drought, with NRW saying sustained high temperatures were causing the condition of the natural environment to "deteriorate".There are no official droughts currently in Northern Ireland.Scotland does not declare droughts but monitors "water scarcity". Several areas of eastern Scotland are now in the most extreme category of "significant scarcity".Rivers, reservoirs and groundwater - how are supplies?Our three main sources of water are rivers, reservoirs and from deep underground. Following the hot, dry weather, the EA has said nearly 80% of England's rivers are seeing flows below normal or lower.Some river flows are around the lowest on record, including the River Thames at Reading and the River Cam at Dernford, Cambridgeshire. "Without significant rainfall we could see increasing impacts on wildlife, agriculture and water resources as the summer progresses," said Steve Turner, a hydrologist at the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology (UKCEH).Meanwhile, reservoirs are a crucial part of water supplies and levels in Wales, Northern Ireland and Scotland are all in a reasonable position, according to the latest available data. But figures up to 21 July show England's reservoirs are below average levels for the time of year. South-east England relies more heavily on groundwater than reservoirs.Groundwater originates as rainfall and is naturally stored beneath the surface in the pore spaces and fractures in rocks. In June, groundwater levels were generally at or just below normal, having been topped up by winter rainfall but depleted by a drier spring in most regions.But water can flow more slowly through some rock types than others, sometimes taking years to fully respond to current conditions.These groundwater stores "respond more slowly to changes in the climate than rivers, which is why they provide a useful buffer during periods of drought", said Prof Alan MacDonald of the British Geological Survey.It is why groundwater droughts in the south of England generally take a longer time to develop but can be longer-lasting if they do occur.Is climate change to blame?Droughts are complex phenomena, driven by a mix of natural and human causes.The Met Office expects the UK to experience drier summers on average in future as the world warms, though there has been no clear trend so far.But rising temperatures can play a more direct role by drawing extra moisture from the soil via evaporation."A warmer atmosphere is thirstier for moisture and this can mean water in the soil, rivers and reservoirs are depleted more effectively, leading to more rapidly onsetting droughts, heatwaves and wildfires," said Richard Allan, professor of climate science at the University of Reading.But there are other factors that determine whether dry conditions lead to water shortages, including how we use water.In a landmark review into the water sector of England and Wales, water companies were criticised for historic underinvestment in water infrastructure.As part of plans to address water shortages, the government and water companies are planning nine new reservoirs for England by 2050, in addition to one under construction at Havant Thicket in Hampshire.But the EA has warned that measures to tackle

articles.summary: AC Milan and Italy great Franco Baresi has died at the age of 66, the Italian club announces.

articles.summaryZh: 意大利AC米兰俱乐部宣布，意大利伟大球员弗兰科·巴雷西去世，享年66岁。

contentParagraphs.en: Baresi formed part of one of European football's most celebrated defences alongside Paolo Maldini, Alessandro Costacurta and Mauro Tassotti. He also lifted four Supercoppa Italianas, two European Super Cups and the Intercontinental Cup twice. In the 1994 World Cup, he returned from a knee injury to play in the final and largely nullified the threat of Brazil's Romario and Bebeto in a 0-0 draw.It was the first World Cup final to be decided by a shootout and Baresi missed the first penalty, with Brazil eventually winning it 3-2. Baresi had surgery in August 2025 to remove a lung nodule, and his last public appearance was at the San Siro Stadium for the Winter Olympics opening ceremony in February. In a statement on X, AC Milan wrote: "Milan is in tears following the passing of Franco Baresi. His example and integrity will be forever etched into the club's DNA, just as his iconic number 6 shirt is." In a further post on the club's website,, external they added: "Announcing the loss of someone who embodied the heart and soul of AC Milan is incredibly difficult. But everyone at the club and all the Milanisti must live up to Franco Baresi's memory."In memory of Franco, we stand united, knowing he'll guide and push us throughout our Rossoneri journey. Forever. Because Baresi is forever." Maldini, 58, who also spent his entire career at Milan, paid tribute to his former team-mate, writing on Instagram:, external "Today, I feel the same way I did whenever - for whatever reason - you couldn't take the field alongside us: how will we manage without our captain?"You taught me to fight until my very last breath, and showed me the meaning of devotion to the jersey and the true value of leadership."You protected me when I was a child, guided me as a young man, and inspired me as an adult. "You were the greatest footballer I ever had the honour of playing with."Former Italy goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon shared memories of his debut for Parma competing against Baresi as a 17-year-old in 1995. He wrote: "For a boy my age, finding myself on the field against champions like him was something incredible. From that day on, I had an even clearer understanding of what it meant to represent football with class, leadership and respect." Inter Milan said:, external "Farewell to Franco Baresi, protagonist of the great clashes in the Milan derby and one of the figures who most defined the history of the rivalry. "Captain, team man and flagbearer of AC Milan, he lived every match-up with Inter between competition and respect, within a challenge that wrote unforgettable pages of Italian soccer."Inter Milan manager Cristian Chivu said Baresi's death "is a sad day for the whole world, he represented being one of the greats in the history of football".Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni said Baresi "was not only one of the greatest champions in (Italian) sports history, but also an example of loyalty, seriousness, and dedication".The head of the Italian football federation (FICG), Giovanni Malago, praised Baresi for the "romantic choice" of staying loyal to AC Milan throughout his career, "which rightfully made him enter the hearts of the fans and millions of Italians."Everyone is hurting, it is a very sad day. Franco Baresi is a legend in Italy, one of the last so-called 'flags' - a one-club player, a player who has only worn one shirt for his entire career.After 15 years as AC Milan captain, his shirt had already been retired so no-one will ever wear the number six again - it shows how important he was for Milan, a symbol of the city.At AC Milan they called him 'Piscinin' - it means a fragile, thin youngster in Milan dialect. That was his nickname when he started back in the 1970s and it was given to him by a famous Italian journalist called Gianni Brera.He had a trial at Inter when he was 12 and his brother Beppe was already at the club, but they rejected him. He ended up at AC Milan that way. But even Inter are mourning, his value has been recognised by all opponents as he is a legend not only for AC Milan. Find me a fan who didn't like or recognise the value of Franco Baresi - it is not going to happen. That is how loved he was.He played alongside some of the biggest champions, Marco van Basten, Paolo Maldini, Ruud Gullit, Frank Rijkaard and he was always at the same level. Baresi was one of the immortal AC Milan players.He won three European Cups, but there were also some sad times - the World Cup in 1994 and the penalty miss. He couldn't play for much of the tournament given the injury he suffered at the beginning, but he made a speedy recovery to play a great game in the final against Brazil.To then miss a penalty in the shootout was a very sad moment for the whole of Italy. But we have never been angry, because Franco Baresi was one of the pillars of the team and the fact he recovered to play in the final was simply inhuman.And in 1989, he finished second in the Ballon d'Or to his team-mate Van Basten - back then, it was inconceivable a defender could win the Ballon d'Or, but Baresi got that close and deserved to win it for the player he was, the quality he had and all he represented - his leadership, importance, quality and his belonging to a club. He deserved that recognition.
contentParagraphs.zh: 巴雷西与保罗·马尔蒂尼、亚历山德罗·科斯塔库塔和毛罗·塔索蒂一起组成了欧洲足坛最著名的防守之一。他还四次夺得意大利超级杯冠军、两次欧洲超级杯冠军和两次洲际杯冠军。 1994年世界杯，他膝伤复出参加决赛，并在0-0战平巴西队罗马里奥和贝贝托的比赛中基本化解了威胁。这是世界杯决赛第一次以点球决胜负，巴雷西罚丢了第一个点球，最终巴西队以3-2获胜。巴雷西于 2025 年 8 月接受了肺结节切除手术，他最后一次公开露面是在 2 月份的圣西罗体育场参加冬奥会开幕式。 AC米兰在X的一份声明中写道：“米兰在弗朗哥·巴雷西去世后流下了眼泪。他的榜样和正直将永远铭刻在俱乐部的DNA中，就像他标志性的6号球衣一样。”在俱乐部网站上的另一篇帖子中，外部人士补充道：“宣布失去一位体现AC米兰核心和灵魂的人是非常困难的。但俱乐部的每个人以及所有米兰球员都必须不辜负弗朗哥·巴雷西的记忆。”为了纪念弗朗哥，我们团结一致，知道他将在整个红黑军团的旅程中指导和推动我们。永远。因为巴雷西是永恒的。”现年 58 岁的马尔蒂尼也在米兰度过了他的整个职业生涯，他在 Instagram 上向他的前队友致敬：“今天，我的感受与每当你无法与我们并肩作战时的感觉一样，无论出于何种原因：如果没有我们的队长，我们将如何应对？”“你教会了我战斗到最后一口气，并向我展示了对球衣奉献的意义和领导力的真正价值。”孩子，在我年轻时引导我，在我成年后激励我。 “你是我有幸共事过的最伟大的足球运动员。”前意大利门将吉安路易吉·布冯分享了他1995年17岁时代表帕尔马首次亮相对阵巴雷西的回忆。他写道：“对于我这个年纪的男孩来说，发现自己在球场上对阵像他这样的冠军是一件令人难以置信的事情。从那天起，我更加清楚地理解了以阶级、领导力和尊重代表足球意味着什么。”国际米兰方面表示：“告别了弗朗哥·巴雷西，他是米兰德比大战的主角，也是最能定义米兰德比历史的人物之一。作为AC米兰的队长、队友和旗手，他在与国际米兰的每场比赛中都经历了竞争与尊重，在一场挑战中写下了意大利足球令人难忘的一页。”意大利总理乔治亚·梅洛尼表示，巴雷西“不仅是（意大利）体育史上最伟大的冠军之一，也是忠诚、认真和奉献的典范”。意大利足协主席乔瓦尼·马拉戈称赞巴雷西在整个职业生涯中忠于AC米兰的“浪漫选择”，“这理所当然地让他走进了球迷和数百万球迷的心中”。意大利人。“每个人都在受伤，这是非常悲伤的一天。弗朗哥·巴雷西是意大利的传奇人物，最后的所谓‘旗帜’之一——一个单一俱乐部的球员，一个整个职业生涯只穿一件球衣的球员。在担任AC米兰队长15年后，他的球衣已经退役，所以没有人会再穿6号球衣——这表明了他对米兰这座城市的象征有多么重要。在AC米兰，他们称他为“Piscinin”——它在米兰方言中，这是他的绰号，是一位名叫贾尼·布雷拉的意大利著名记者给他起的。他12岁时曾在国际米兰试训，但他们最终拒绝了他。尽管国际米兰正在哀悼，但他的价值已经得到了所有对手的认可，因为他不仅是AC米兰的传奇人物。不喜欢或不认识弗朗哥·巴雷西的价值——这是不可能的。他曾与一些伟大的冠军球员一起踢球，比如范巴斯滕、保罗·马尔蒂尼、古力特、弗兰克·里杰卡尔德，而他一直是不朽的AC米兰球员之一。他赢得了三座欧洲杯，但也有过一些悲伤的时刻——1994年世界杯和点球错失。考虑到他一开始就受了伤，他参加了大部分比赛，但他很快就康复了，在对阵巴西的决赛中打出了一场精彩的比赛。在点球大战中错失点球对整个意大利来说都是一个非常悲伤的时刻，但我们从来没有生气，因为弗兰科·巴雷西是球队的支柱之一，而他在决赛中恢复上场的事实简直不人道。1989年，他在金球奖上输给了队友范巴斯滕，获得了第二名。在当时，一名后卫能够赢得金球奖是不可想象的，但巴雷西已经如此接近，他理应赢得金球奖，因为他是一名球员，他所拥有的品质和他所代表的一切——他的领导力、重要性、品质和他对俱乐部的归属感，他值得获得这一认可。

articles.title: Teen hackers tell BBC how police are helping them use their skills for good
articles.summary: Cyber Prevent is targeting predominantly boys and young men at risk of being drawn to cyber criminality.
articles.titleZh: 青少年黑客告诉 BBC 警方如何帮助他们利用自己的技能做好事
articles.summaryZh: Cyber​​ Prevent 主要针对有可能陷入网络犯罪的男孩和年轻人。

contentParagraphs.en: Image caption, Lucas said he felt a "sense of achievement" from hackingByJoe TidyWorld Service cyber correspondentLucas was 16 when he got into trouble for hacking his school computers. Twice."It was like a challenge to see if I could," he told the BBC.He wanted access to play games and visit blocked websites so he started tinkering with programming.At one point he even unscrewed the computer tower to take some internal components home for tests."It's quite a sense of achievement when you've succeeded in doing something that two or three trained professionals have spent a lot of time trying to stop you doing," he said. He was close to being expelled - but his worried mother had no idea how serious his actions were.She called the police and invited an officer from the nationwide programme Cyber Choices to their home in rural Cumbria."My mum was like, 'ooh, you've got a detective coming to speak to you, you're in a lot of trouble'," Lucas said."So I was sat at the window waiting. Who's going to come? How much trouble am I going to be in?"PC Sam Cooper knocked on the door earlier this year and has been working with Lucas ever since.Image caption, PC Sam Cooper visits children at their homes to guide them away from cyber-crimeHe explained to Lucas, as he has with dozens of other children, there were real consequences and harm caused by cyber-attacks.Cooper said showing the mostly teenage boys what was legal and not was step one. Then comes positive encouragement over months of one-to-one meetings, usually at their homes."I'll try and find where their interests are and try and divert them towards professional training, qualifications," he said.Cyber Choices, also known as Cyber Prevent, is like a hacker rehab course. It works in parallel with the more well-known Prevent scheme, which identifies potential terror offenders.While at Lucas's house I saw first hand how some of the conversations work. Lucas enthusiastically explained his latest computer experiments and Cooper asked him what software and tools he was using to check they were legitimate.Soon the officer will take Lucas on a visit to the local university where he will be shown the cyber security course with the aim of inspiring him to apply.Image caption, Paul Foster, the NCA's cyber prevention lead, says hacking has become "more of a problem"More than 1,150 cases have been referred to the National Crime Agency (NCA)'s Cyber Choices scheme in the last eight years - nearly 600 of those were in the last three years.Authorities warn teenage hacking groups are playing an increasingly prominent role in serious cyber-attacks.Young, English-speaking hackers have been linked to attacks on major organisations including Transport for London (TfL) and MGM Grand in 2024, and Marks & Spencer and the Co-op in 2025.Individuals are also being increasingly targeted in hacks for their cryptocurrency holdings."It certainly has become more of a problem," said Paul Foster, who leads cyber prevention work at the NCA."Certainly English-speaking, Western world individuals that we know are now more active in cyber-crime."He said young people were engaged with online activity and devices at increasingly young ages exposing them to criminal communities and influences.Police say many young offenders do not initially set out to become criminals. Instead, they often begin by experimenting with technology, testing systems or trying to bypass restrictions before becoming drawn into online communities where hacking is encouraged.'Majority are neurodiverse'The children can come from all over the country and from a range of backgrounds, and Cooper said many be autistic or are neurodiverse."The vast majority of individuals I'm dealing with are neurodiverse," he said."Even if they're not labelled as such... they obviously have more affinity with computers than they do with practical and social reality," he said."Sometimes they can get fixated on certain goals and not listen to any adults around them, so that's where I come in and sit them down and talk to them."In 2023, a high profile teenage hacker called Arion Kurtaj, who had hacked Grand Theft Auto maker Rockstar Games, was deemed unfit to stand trial because he was severely autistic.Two teenage hackers who were jailed earlier this month for the TfL hack were also autistic - which was taken into account by the judge when he sentenced them to five and a half years in prison.Image source, Metropolitan PoliceImage caption, Owen Flowers (left) and Thalha Jubair admitted hacking TfLOne of them, Owen Flowers from Walsall, had been offered a chance to enrol on the Cyber Choices programme when he first got into trouble shortly after he turned 16.He refused to engage with the scheme.Some critics argue that teaching cyber skills to young people who have already shown an interest in hacking risks making them more capable offenders.In another ongoing court case, it emerged a teenager who had been enrolled on the programme was alleged to have gone on to commit further offences.Foster said he understood the concern but believes the alternative would be worse."My fear is that if we didn't give them something like Cyber Choices, where would they get that input and where would that input take them?"The NCA hoped it could intervene before curiosity, talent and online influence turn into serious offending.For Lucas, the fear of having a police officer show up at his door made him rethink things.He admits that if he had not been caught and helped by the scheme he would have carried on pushing boundaries in his exploration of computers and hacking.Meanwhile in Leicestershire, 21-year-old cyber-security professional Izak is another Cyber Choices success story.At 15, he hacked his school computers so he could make graphic designs in Photoshop, but he also found himself drawn into cyber-crime groups online who were making "lots of money".A visit from Leicestershire Police got him on to the programme and helped him see cyber-security as a pos
contentParagraphs.zh: 图片说明：卢卡斯说，他从黑客攻击中感受到了一种“成就感”ByJoe TidyWorld Service 网络通讯员卢卡斯 16 岁时，因黑客入侵学校计算机而陷入麻烦。两次。他告诉 BBC。“这对我来说就像是一个挑战，看看我是否能做到。”他想玩游戏并访问被封锁的网站，所以他开始修改编程。有一次，他甚至拧开了电脑塔，把一些内部组件带回家进行测试。“当你成功地做到了两三个训练有素的专业人员花了很多时间试图阻止你做的事情时，这是一种相当大的成就感，”他说。他差点被开除，但他担心的母亲不知道他的行为有多严重。她报了警，并邀请了全国网络选择项目的一名官员到他们位于坎布里亚乡村的家中。卢卡斯说：“我妈妈说，‘哦，有一名侦探要来找你说话，你有麻烦了’。”“所以我坐在窗边等待。谁会来？我会遇到多少麻烦？”今年早些时候，他敲开了卢卡斯的大门，此后一直与卢卡斯合作。图片说明，警官萨姆·库珀 (Sam Cooper) 到孩子们家中探访，引导他们远离网络犯罪。他向卢卡斯解释，就像他对其他数十名孩子所做的那样，网络攻击会造成真正的后果和伤害。库珀说，第一步是向大多数十几岁的男孩展示什么是合法的，什么是非法的。然后是几个月的一对一会议的积极鼓励，通常是在他们的家里。“我会尝试找到他们的兴趣所在，并尝试将他们转向专业培训和资格认证，”他说。网络选择，也称为网络预防，就像黑客康复课程。它与更知名的预防计划并行工作，该计划识别潜在的恐怖犯罪者。在卢卡斯家里时，我亲眼目睹了一些对话是如何进行的。卢卡斯热情地解释了他最新的计算机实验，库珀问他正在使用什么软件和工具来检查它们的合法性。很快，该官员将带卢卡斯参观当地大学，在那里他将学习网络安全课程，目的是激励他申请。图片说明，NCA 网络预防负责人保罗·福斯特表示，黑客攻击已成为“一个更严重的问题”。在过去 8 年中，已向国家犯罪局 (NCA) 的网络选择计划提交了超过 1,150 起案件近 600 起此类事件发生在过去三年。当局警告青少年黑客组织在严重网络攻击中发挥着越来越重要的作用。年轻的英语黑客与主要组织的攻击有关，包括 2024 年对伦敦交通局 (TfL) 和米高梅大酒店的攻击，以及 2025 年对玛莎百货和合作社的攻击。个人也越来越多地因其持有的加密货币而成为黑客攻击的目标。 NCA 网络预防工作负责人保罗·福斯特 (Paul Foster) 表示：“当然，据我们所知，讲英语的西方世界个人现在在网络犯罪中更加活跃。”他表示，年轻人在年龄越来越小的时候就开始参与网络活动和使用网络设备，这让他们接触到犯罪群体并受到影响。警方表示，许多年轻犯罪者最初并没有打算成为犯罪分子。相反，他们通常会先尝试技术、测试系统或试图绕过限制，然后进入鼓励黑客攻击的在线社区。“大多数人都是神经多元化的”孩子们可能来自全国各地，背景各异，库珀说，他们中的许多人患有自闭症或神经多元化。“我接触到的绝大多数人都是神经多元化的，”他说。“即使他们没有被贴上这样的标签……他们显然对计算机的亲和力比对实际和社交的亲和力更强。他说：“有时候，他们会专注于某些目标，不听周围任何成年人的意见，所以我就进来，让他们坐下来与他们交谈。”2023 年，一位名叫 Arion Kurtaj 的知名青少年黑客入侵了侠盗猎车手制造商 Rockstar Games，被认为不适合接受审判，因为他患有严重自闭症。本月早些时候因伦敦交通局黑客事件而入狱的两名青少年黑客也被认为不适合接受审判。法官在判处他们五年半监禁时考虑到了这一点。图片来源，大都会警察局图片说明，欧文·弗劳尔斯（左）和塔哈·朱贝尔承认黑客攻击伦敦交通局。其中一位来自沃尔索尔的欧文·弗劳尔斯在 16 岁后不久第一次遇到麻烦时，曾获得参加网络选择计划的机会。他拒绝参与该计划。一些批评者认为，向那些患有自闭症的年轻人教授网络技能已经表现出对黑客风险的兴趣，使他们更有能力犯罪。在另一起正在进行的法庭案件中，一名参加该计划的青少年被指控继续犯下进一步的罪行。福斯特说，他理解这种担忧，但相信替代方案会更糟。“我担心的是，如果我们不给他们类似网络选择的东西，他们会从哪里获得信息，这些信息又会把他们带到哪里？”NCA 希望在好奇心、才能和网络影响力变成严重犯罪之前进行干预。卢卡斯，对警察出现在他家门口的恐惧让他重新思考事情。他承认，如果他没有被这个计划抓住并得到帮助，他会继续突破计算机和黑客探索的界限。与此同时，在莱斯特郡，21 岁的网络安全专业人士伊扎克是网络选择的另一个成功案例。15 岁时，他入侵了学校的计算机，以便可以在 Photoshop 中进行图形设计，但他也发现自己被卷入了网上网络犯罪团体，赚了“很多钱”。莱斯特郡警方的一次拜访让他加入了这个项目，并帮助他将网络安全视为一种优势

contentParagraphs.en: The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage hit 6.66% this week, according to the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., commonly known as Freddie Mac.
contentParagraphs.zh: 根据联邦住房贷款抵押公司（俗称房地美）的数据，本周 30 年期固定利率抵押贷款平均利率达到 6.66%。

contentParagraphs.en: That's the highest it's reached in a year — at the end of last July, the average rate was 6.72%. The biblically ominous 6.66% figure could strike fear into homebuyers because it's a sign that home ownership is becoming less affordable.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这是一年来的最高水平——去年 7 月底的平均利率为 6.72%。 6.66%这个不祥的数字可能会让购房者感到恐惧，因为这表明住房所有权变得越来越难以负担。

contentParagraphs.en: Last summer, rates were falling, and the decline continued into early 2026. Rates even dipped below 6% in February, raising hopes that this would unlock a tepid housing market, in which home seekers have been reluctant to buy and homeowners have been loath to give up lower pandemic-era rates.
contentParagraphs.zh: 去年夏天，利率开始下降，下降趋势一直持续到 2026 年初。2 月份利率甚至跌破 6%，引发了人们对这将开启不温不火的房地产市场的希望，在这个市场中，购房者一直不愿购房，房主也不愿放弃疫情期间较低的利率。

contentParagraphs.en: But then the war with Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz raised the price of oil. Rising oil prices meant more expensive shipping costs, which drove up the price of just about everything. That in turn drove up the yield on the 10-year Treasury note, a kind of security that is backed by the U.S. government. It's considered an indicator of which way other interest rates are trending — and mortgage rates closely follow.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但随后与伊朗的战争和霍尔木兹海峡的关闭提高了石油价格。油价上涨意味着运输成本上涨，从而推高了几乎所有商品的价格。这反过来推高了十年期国债的收益率，这是一种由美国政府支持的证券。它被认为是其他利率趋势的指标，抵押贷款利率也紧随其后。

contentParagraphs.en: "Oil prices always swing mortgage rates," said Kara Ng, senior economist at Zillow. "You get a real-time read every time you go to a gas pump about what it means to buy a home."
contentParagraphs.zh: Zillow 高级经济学家 Kara Ng 表示：“油价总是会影响抵押贷款利率。” “每次你去加油站时，你都会实时了解到买房意味着什么。”

contentParagraphs.en: The average for a gallon of regular on Thursday was $4.10, according to AAA, about $1.11 higher than before the war began.
contentParagraphs.zh: 根据 AAA 的数据，周四每加仑普通汽油的平均价格为 4.10 美元，比战争开始前高出约 1.11 美元。

contentParagraphs.en: Kate Wood, a housing expert for the financial advice website NerdWallet, said that because the fighting in Iran has gone through so many pauses and restarts, investors' fears won't be calmed without a significant signal that the conflict is coming to an end.
contentParagraphs.zh: 金融咨询网站NerdWallet的住房专家凯特·伍德(Kate Wood)表示，由于伊朗的战斗经历了如此多的停顿和重启，如果没有冲突即将结束的重大信号，投资者的担忧就不会平息。

contentParagraphs.en: "The best bet would be a decisive, conclusive, actually-sticks end to fighting in Iran," Wood said. But, she added, even then investors could remain skeptical: "Markets might be a little bit once bitten, twice shy."
contentParagraphs.zh: 伍德说：“最好的选择是果断、决定性地、切实地结束伊朗的战斗。”但她补充说，即便如此，投资者仍可能持怀疑态度：“市场可能会有点一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳的感觉。”

contentParagraphs.en: Those same investors were also spooked after the Federal Reserve on Wednesday signaled that an interest rate hike could be on the way in September, even as it held its benchmark interest rate steady for now.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美联储周三表示，尽管目前基准利率保持稳定，但可能会在 9 月份加息，这些投资者也感到惊慌。

contentParagraphs.en: Three of the central bank's rate-setting committee members voted for a hike. That wasn't enough to alter the outcome, but markets saw the rare split as indication that a higher rate could be coming in the near future.
contentParagraphs.zh: 三名央行利率制定委员会成员投票支持加息。这还不足以改变结果，但市场认为这种罕见的分歧表明不久的将来可能会出现更高的利率。

contentParagraphs.en: The sticker price for homes has also contributed to the tepid housing market. Sales have barely moved over the last three years, according to the National Association of Realtors. In June, the average existing home sold for more than $440,000, while sales themselves declined 2.4% from a year earlier.
contentParagraphs.zh: 房屋标价也导致房地产市场不温不火。根据全国房地产经纪人协会的数据，过去三年销售量几乎没有变化。 6 月份，现房平均售价超过 44 万美元，而销售额同比下降 2.4%。

articles.title: Here's how 'parasite' went from a laughing matter to a serious biological threat
articles.summary: Odysseus did not face the parasite Cyclospora in his 10-year journey home. But the word "parasite" originated as a popular character trope in Greek literature.
articles.titleZh: 这就是“寄生虫”如何从一个可笑的事情变成一个严重的生物威胁
articles.summaryZh: 奥德修斯在长达10年的回家路上，并没有遇到寄生虫环孢子虫。但“寄生虫”一词起源于希腊文学中的一个流行人物比喻。

contentParagraphs.en: Spinach is displayed for sale on shelves at a Target store on July 23, 2026 in Austin, Texas.
contentParagraphs.zh: 2026 年 7 月 23 日，得克萨斯州奥斯汀市 Target 商店的货架上展示着待售的菠菜。

contentParagraphs.en: Cyclospora and Christopher Nolan's nearly three hour adaptation of The Odyssey have something in common — parasites.
contentParagraphs.zh: 《环孢菌》和克里斯托弗·诺兰近三小时的《奥德赛》改编版有一些共同点——寄生虫。

contentParagraphs.en: For Cyclospora, that connection is easy to make. The microscopic parasite causes cyclosporiasis, the intestinal illness that has sickened thousands of Americans.
contentParagraphs.zh: 对于环孢子虫来说，这种联系很容易建立。这种微小的寄生虫会引起环孢子虫病，这种肠道疾病已经使成千上万的美国人患病。

contentParagraphs.en: And while Odysseus does not face an intestinal parasite on his long journey home — though his voyage was still quite miserable — he encountered another kind when he returned to Ithaca. Those were the suitors who had taken over his home, courting his wife Penelope. They embodied a popular character trope in ancient Greek writing: one that originated as a form of comic relief.
contentParagraphs.zh: 虽然奥德修斯在漫长的归途中并没有遇到肠道寄生虫——尽管他的旅程仍然相当痛苦——但当他回到伊萨卡岛时，他遇到了另一种寄生虫。这些追求者接管了他的家，向他的妻子佩内洛普求爱。它们体现了古希腊文学中一种流行的人物比喻：一种起源于喜剧浮雕的形式。

contentParagraphs.en: As part of NPR's "Word of the Week" series, we're explaining how the word "parasite" started as a joke and became anything but funny.
contentParagraphs.zh: 作为 NPR“本周词汇”系列的一部分，我们将解释“寄生虫”这个词如何从一个笑话开始，然后变得一点也不有趣。

contentParagraphs.en: A witty dinner guest in ancient Greece
contentParagraphs.zh: 古希腊一位机智的晚餐客人

contentParagraphs.en: The original definition of parasite or "parasitos" comes from Greek, literally translating to "alongside of (para) grain or wheat (sitos)."
contentParagraphs.zh: 寄生虫或“parasitos”的原始定义来自希腊语，字面意思是“与（para）谷物或小麦（sitos）一起”。

contentParagraphs.en: The ancient Greeks used the word to describe someone, usually poor, who would entertain a wealthy person for food. The sentiment became an "institution" in ancient Greece and Rome, said Richard Martin, a classics professor at Stanford University. It turned into a comedic stock character, he said.
contentParagraphs.zh: 古希腊人用这个词来形容那些招待富人吃饭的人，通常是穷人。斯坦福大学古典学教授理查德·马丁说，这种情绪在古希腊和罗马已成为一种“制度”。他说，它变成了一个喜剧角色。

contentParagraphs.en: "You should always expect the parasite to come on stage and do crazy stuff," Martin said.
contentParagraphs.zh: “你应该时刻预料到寄生虫会出现并做出疯狂的事情，”马丁说。

contentParagraphs.en: The parasite is a jokester figure who tries to derail the main character and cause confusion, with comedic names like "Bread-Chewer," Martin said. The character could also lean towards the "sleazy" side. The character was big in "New Comedy," he said, a "kind of domestic sitcom style" humor that started in fourth century B.C., specifically from the Greek playwright, Menander.
contentParagraphs.zh: 马丁说，寄生虫是一个爱开玩笑的人物，试图让主角出轨并造成混乱，其喜剧名字如“嚼面包者”。这个角色也可能倾向于“低俗”的一面。他说，这个角色在《新喜剧》中很重要，这是一种始于公元前四世纪的“家庭情景喜剧风格”幽默，特别是来自希腊剧作家米南德。

contentParagraphs.en: For a modern example, Martin points to the comedy duo Abbott and Costello from the 1940s and '50s. They're known for the classic "Who's on First" comedy sketch.
contentParagraphs.zh: 马丁以 20 世纪 40 年代和 50 年代的喜剧二人组阿博特和科斯特洛为例，举了一个现代的例子。他们以经典的“谁先上”喜剧小品而闻名。

contentParagraphs.en: Craig Jendza, an associate professor of Ancient Greek and Roman Studies at Denison University, said that to audiences, the humor of the parasite laid in their uncanny ability to do anything they possibly could for food. Take, for example, plucking dandruff off another person's head, he said.
contentParagraphs.zh: 丹尼森大学古希腊罗马研究副教授克雷格·詹扎 (Craig Jendza) 表示，对观众来说，寄生虫的幽默之处在于它们具有不可思议的能力，可以为食物做任何事情。他说，以拔掉别人头上的头皮屑为例。

contentParagraphs.en: In The Odyssey, the freeloading suitors in Odysseus' home are also considered parasites — without the "comedic overtones," Jendza said. That's also implicit in the repetition of breaking "Zeus' law" that's often cited in the Nolan movie. "That's what's going on with the parasite," Jendza said. "He's exploiting those social obligations… and he's doing it for his own self-interest."
contentParagraphs.zh: 詹扎说，在《奥德赛》中，奥德修斯家里那些贪图便宜的追求者也被认为是寄生虫——没有“喜剧色彩”。这也隐含在诺兰电影中经常引用的违反“宙斯法则”的重复中。 “这就是寄生虫的情况，”詹扎说。 “他正在利用这些社会义务……他这样做是为了自己的利益。”

contentParagraphs.en: In that sense, Martin said, The Odyssey was ahead of his time: "[The suitors] are parasites in the modern sense: They give nothing, but they take everything."
contentParagraphs.zh: 马丁说，从这个意义上说，《奥德赛》领先于他的时代：“[追求者]是现代意义上的寄生虫：他们什么也不给予，但他们却夺走了一切。”

contentParagraphs.en: A biological threat
contentParagraphs.zh: 生物威胁

contentParagraphs.en: Today, most people know of a parasite as a tiny organism, one that needs a host to live. "A parasite is something that is preying on something else," Craig Hedberg, a professor in the School of Public Health at the University of Minnesota.
contentParagraphs.zh: 如今，大多数人都知道寄生虫是一种微小的生物体，需要宿主才能生存。 “寄生虫是一种捕食其他东西的东西，”明尼苏达大学公共卫生学院教授克雷格·赫德伯格说。

contentParagraphs.en: There's a plausible linguistic pathway from ancient Greece, said Brian Joseph, a distinguished university professor emeritus of linguistics at The Ohio State University, since they also saw the parasite character as a "freeloader."
contentParagraphs.zh: 俄亥俄州立大学杰出的语言学名誉教授布莱恩·约瑟夫（Brian Joseph）表示，有一条似乎来自古希腊的语言途径，因为他们也将寄生虫角色视为“贪图便宜的人”。

contentParagraphs.en: Martin, the Stanford professor, said doctors up until at least the 20th century understood Greek and Latin — so he can see how the ancient definition could come to describe "the kind of bug that feeds off another one." This new definition just loses the humor.
contentParagraphs.zh: 斯坦福大学教授马丁表示，至少在 20 世纪之前，医生们都懂得希腊语和拉丁语，因此他可以看到古代的定义如何来描述“以另一种虫子为食的虫子”。这个新定义只是失去了幽默感。

contentParagraphs.en: "Bring back the funny parasite," Martin said.
contentParagraphs.zh: “把有趣的寄生虫带回来，”马丁说。

contentParagraphs.en: That brings us to the microscopic gastrointestinal parasite that's wreaking havoc right now: Cyclospora, which has caused outbreaks in at least nine states. It infects the small intestine and causes excessive diarrhea, fatigue and cramping for several weeks, said Gerardo Lopez, an associate professor of food safety and environmental microbiology at the University of Arizona.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这让我们看到了目前正在造成严重破坏的微小胃肠道寄生虫：环孢子虫，它已在至少九个州引发了疫情。亚利桑那大学食品安全和环境微生物学副教授杰拉多·洛佩兹说，它会感染小肠，导致持续数周的过度腹泻、疲劳和痉挛。

contentParagraphs.en: Like the Greek parasites, Cyclospora does like to eat: "They are gaining nutrients from us," Lopez said. And their ability to attach to foods like iceberg lettuce and live inside humans is "brilliant," he said.
contentParagraphs.zh: 就像希腊寄生虫一样，环孢子虫也喜欢吃东西：“它们从我们身上获取营养，”洛佩兹说。他说，它们附着在卷心生菜等食物上并生活在人体体内的能力“非常出色”。

contentParagraphs.en: But unlike the literary figures, "there's nothing funny about it," Lopez said. Hedberg, the University of Minnesota professor, agrees.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但与文学人物不同的是，“这没有什么好笑的，”洛佩兹说。明尼苏达大学教授赫德伯格对此表示赞同。

contentParagraphs.en: "We have a lot of fun talking about diarrhea, but diarrhea isn't a fun thing to actually experience on a personal level," Hedberg said.
contentParagraphs.zh: “我们很高兴谈论腹泻，但在个人层面上实际经历腹泻并不是一件有趣的事情，”赫德伯格说。
